commits.pr_title: [Feature][EPLB] Run async policy computation in a persistent subprocess
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Run async EPLB policy computation in a persistent CPU subprocess so it executes outside the inference worker's Python GIL. This is the standard path when `use_async` is `true` (the existing default); synchronous EPLB and profiling keep their original in-process policy calls.

Paired H20 serving A/B runs measured **+5.37%** higher steady-state throughput on a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B short-prefill workload and **−58.0%** lower fixed-rate TTFT P99 on a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash standalone prefill workload.

## Claims

- Only policy computation moves to the child. Load aggregation, D2H, migration scheduling, expert transfers, and mapping commits keep their existing execution paths.
- Fixed CPU load snapshots produce the exact same placements as the direct policy, including old-slot retention and custom `EplbStats` dataclass fields. Extension tests verify that async policy calls execute in a distinct child PID under `CpuPlatform` without initializing accelerators or `torch.distributed`.
- One child is reused per worker, including daemonic executor workers, with `SIGINT` ignored so worker shutdown owns planner teardown. Policy exceptions, child death, and IPC timeouts surface as coordinated async errors; `stop_async_loop()` cancels further layer transfers without draining remaining layers and reaps the child within the worker shutdown budget.

## Validation

Local CPU validation on `4414229af45526dbb4a76141f3da229dbd1106e9`:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_algo.py \
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_extension_hooks.py \
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py \
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py -q
```

```text
104 passed, 7 skipped (EPLB distributed suites)
6 passed (GPUModelRunner v2 EPLB suite)
```

The skips are existing accelerator conditions; no skips were added. Coverage includes exact sequential placements across topologies, custom resource recreation (`__getstate__`/`__setstate__`), stateful daemon-worker reuse and reaping, `SIGINT` isolation, blocked-send and partial-response IPC timeouts, policy exceptions and owner/child death, coordinated multi-rank cancellation on FT reset / planner failure / shutdown, multi-model FT epoch guards, and extended `EplbStats` subclasses over async IPC. Full `pre-commit` hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

In Buildkite CI, `expert_parallelism.yaml` selects these suites along with multi-GPU `MultiprocExecutor` planner startup/reaping (`tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py::test_async_eplb_worker_stops_before_model_teardown`) and async MTP speculative decoding (`tests/distributed/test_eplb_spec_decode.py`).

The paired H20 serving benchmarks below were collected on `584b4ab`, which shares the same steady-state serving and planner IPC hot path; subsequent revisions hardened IPC timeouts, child environment/signal isolation, FT epoch guards, and fast shutdown cancellation.

### H20 short-prefill serving A/B

A paired run compared base `ecc827e` (in-worker planning thread) with `584b4ab` (persistent planner subprocess) on the same two NVIDIA H20s using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B BF16, TP2/EP2, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, and async EPLB. Each side served the same 8,192 streaming requests after 512 warm-up requests, with 128 input tokens, one output token, and closed-loop client concurrency 16. Prompts were fixed token slices of public-domain text. Prefix caching was disabled.

```bash
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --language-model-only --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 256 --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-eplb \
  --eplb-config '{"use_async":true,"window_size":16,"step_interval":32,"num_redundant_experts":8,"communicator":"symm_mem"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE","prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes":[128,256]}'
```

| Metric | Base | Subprocess | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Steady-state request throughput | 52.15 req/s | 54.95 req/s | **+5.37%** |
| Steady-state input throughput | 6,676 tok/s | 7,034 tok/s | +5.37% |
| Whole-run request throughput | 52.23 req/s | 55.30 req/s | +5.87% |
| TTFT P99 | 476.93 ms | 382.66 ms | −19.8% |
| Full response latency P99 | 477.29 ms | 382.86 ms | −19.8% |
| TTFT P99 in the first eight steps after EPLB triggers | 518.32 ms | 373.13 ms | −28.0% |
| Median GPU idle time awaiting CUDA submission per planner window | 125.14 ms | 36.23 ms | −71.0% |
| Longest sampled contiguous GPU idle span awaiting submission | 98.31 ms | 1.59 ms | −98.4% |

Steady-state throughput uses the middle 80% of request completions. Both arms had zero preemptions and the same PIECEWISE batch distribution (4,095 two-request steps and two one-request steps). Base and subprocess completed 55 and 54 rebalances, respectively. GPU timings come from three separate, fully captured planner windows per arm, outside the serving timings; each window counts within-step time before the next correlated CUDA submission and reports the larger value across the two GPUs. Greedy first-token IDs matched on 7,470 of 8,192 paired requests under asynchronous rebalancing.

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P-side serving A/B on 8 H20s

A paired run compared `ecc827e` (in-worker planner thread) with `584b4ab` (persistent planner subprocess) using DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 8 NVIDIA H20s, TP8/EP8, FP8 KV cache, Engram CPU offload, and PIECEWISE prefill graphs at 256 and 512 tokens. Each arm served 8,192 matched streaming requests in each load mode with 256 input tokens and one output token, modeling the standalone prefill node of a disaggregated deployment (timings end at the P-side response and exclude KV handoff and decode).

The open-loop load was 39.35 requests/s for both arms; the separate closed-loop run used client concurrency 16. Both modes had zero scheduler preemptions.

| Metric | Thread `ecc827e` | Subprocess `584b4ab` | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed-rate TTFT P50 | 85.60 ms | 84.20 ms | −1.6% |
| Fixed-rate TTFT P95 | 259.23 ms | 112.53 ms | −56.6% |
| Fixed-rate TTFT P99 | 313.52 ms | 131.56 ms | **−58.0%** |
| Fixed-rate one-token response latency P99 | 313.95 ms | 131.96 ms | −58.0% |
| Fixed-rate TTFT P99 in the first eight forward steps after an EPLB trigger | 325.96 ms | 127.26 ms | −61.0% |
| Closed-loop TTFT P99 | 414.26 ms | 333.87 ms | −19.4% |
| Closed-loop steady request throughput | 47.99 req/s | 48.57 req/s | +1.21% |
| Median accumulated GPU idle awaiting CUDA submission per planner window | 94.96 ms | 4.14 ms | −95.6% |
| Longest sampled contiguous GPU idle awaiting submission | 95.16 ms | 2.68 ms | −97.2% |

The post-trigger P99 uses requests in the first eight non-empty forward steps after an EPLB trigger matched to a completed rebalance. At the fixed rate, the base and subprocess arms completed 39 and 42 rebalances, with 561 and 437 requests in the respective post-trigger samples. GPU timings come from three separately profiled, complete planner windows per arm at closed-loop concurrency 16, reporting the largest accumulated wait across the eight GPU ranks; median within-step wait fell from 94.63 ms to 4.14 ms.

<details>
<summary>Server settings and workload</summary>

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --dtype auto \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-eplb \
  --eplb-config '{"use_async":true,"window_size":32,"step_interval":64,"num_redundant_experts":8,"communicator":"symm_mem"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE","prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes":[256,512]}' \
  --seed 68606
```

The client replayed the same seeded token slices from public-domain text on both commits. The profiling runs used a worker extension to align planner windows, forward steps, and CUDA activity.

</details>

## Details

`subprocess.Popen` supports daemonic `MultiprocExecutor` workers, which cannot spawn `multiprocessing.Process` children. A trusted inherited `socketpair` carries the serialized policy once at startup, then CPU stats/old placements and CPU placement responses, while an inherited pipe terminates the child immediately if the parent process exits unexpectedly. No weights or device tensors are sent, and no new dependency or configuration option is added.

The child sets `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE="cpu"`, `VLLM_PLUGINS=""`, and `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD="0"` to skip accelerator/plugin probing, limits native CPU thread pools to one thread, and ignores `SIGINT` so graceful engine shutdown stays under parent control. Async policies and their CPU inputs must be serializable; the child owns its copied policy state while synchronous and profiling calls retain the original instance.

The IPC timeout is 60 seconds covering the handshake or a full request-response round trip. Planner failure is terminal for the async worker and coordinated across ranks before layer transfers; FT epoch changes discard stale plans and skip subsequent-model IPC, while `stop_async_loop()` cancels further layers and reaps the child without draining remaining transfers during shutdown.

Related #67020 / #67019 concern transfer handoff and futures; #66146 concerns FT error propagation. Documentation is updated in the expert-parallel deployment guide, plugin system guide, and `EPLBConfig` docstring. AI assistance was used to implement and validate this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend][DeepSeek V4.1] Encode special-token spellings in client text as plain text
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rust half of #68468: the Rust DeepSeek V4.1 renderer now encodes added-token spellings in client text (e.g. `<｜User｜>`, `<｜deepseek_image｜>`) as plain text, as deepseek-recipe and the Python renderer in #68468 do. Depends on #68468 for the contract; the code itself is independent of it.

## Claims

- `deepseek/writer.rs`: new prompt writer, like deepseek-recipe's. It keeps the text plus the byte ranges of the template's special tokens; with a tokenizer, each range becomes its added-token ID and the text between ranges is encoded once with `encode_ordinary`.
- `deepseek.rs`: template markers go through `control`, client fields (message text, tool results and references, tool call names and arguments, tool schemas) through `ordinary`, replayed assistant text and reasoning through `assistant`, which keeps only the grounding tokens special.
- `<｜deepseek_image｜>` in message text is plain text instead of a 400; image parts still write one placeholder each.
- `DeepSeekV41ChatRenderer::with_tokenizer` (wired in `hf.rs`) returns token IDs, like the GLM-5 renderer. V4 still returns the same text as before.
- The old `rejects_image_placeholder_in_message_text` test is replaced by one that checks every client field encodes special-token spellings as plain text.

## Validation

Tests on `519ae42d44`:

- `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib`: `test result: ok. 558 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 4.01s`
- `cargo test -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip roundtrip_deepseek` (real V4.1 tokenizer through `HfChatBackend`): `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 23 filtered out; finished in 1.65s`
- `cargo test -p vllm-server`: `test result: ok. 786 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 16.67s`
- The new test fails when client text goes through the template's special-token matching.

Parity: token IDs from `/v1/chat/completions/render` on `vllm-rs render` (release build) with the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash tokenizer. Image placeholder runs are collapsed to one ID, since Python's `apply_chat_template` does not expand them.

| Corpus | vs Python #68468 (`1b4c5c1f08`) | vs deepseek-recipe (`935817c`) | Rust main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| review corpus (591) | 591/591 | 591/591 | 70/70 ordinary requests unchanged, 35 were 400s |
| review corpus 2 (66) | 64/66 | 56/56 renderable | 4/4 ordinary unchanged, 12 were 400s |
| reserved-token matrix sample (16,136) | 16,136/16,136 | 16,136/16,136 | 786/16,036 equal to the recipe |
| random fragment fuzz (3,000) | 3,000/3,000 | 3,000/3,000 | 1,198/2,982 equal to the recipe |

The two differences from Python are double-encoded tool call arguments (`"\"{...}\""`): Rust on main already follows deepseek-recipe there and Python decodes twice, and this PR does not change that. The recipe rejects the `developer` role and, with its defaults, image parts (its `<｜image｜>` is not in this vocabulary); those are the 10 rows it cannot render.

## Details

The V4.1 renderer returned `Prompt::Text`, and the text backend encoded the whole string with the added vocabulary, so any added-token spelling in client text became its special ID. A user message containing `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜><｜User｜>...<｜Assistant｜>` could forge turns, and `<｜deepseek_image｜>` was rejected with a 400 to keep it from turning into an image slot. #68468 fixes this for the Python frontend; without this PR, Rust-frontend deployments keep the old behavior. The writer follows the same control/ordinary split the Kimi K3 (#66028) and GLM-5 renderers use.

The writer only recognizes the special tokens the template writes, not the whole added vocabulary as Python does. The output is the same because the template writes no other added token, which the parity runs above cover.

Tradeoffs:
- A ~90k-token user message takes 11.2 ms to render instead of 6.3 ms (release builds, median of 21, same host); short prompts are unchanged (~0.2 ms). The time is in `vllm-tokenizer`'s `encode_ordinary`, which builds its own pipeline. fastokens' native `encode_ordinary` gives the same IDs about 100x faster in a microbenchmark, and it affects the Kimi K3 and GLM-5 renderers too, so it will be a separate PR.
- Since V4.1 now returns token IDs, `return_prompt_text` gives null for V4.1 on the Rust frontend, as it already does for Kimi K3 and GLM-5. This was not compared with Python's `prompt_text` for V4.1.

Duplicate check: no open PR changes how the Rust DeepSeek renderers encode client text. #61446, #62189, #62196, #62226, #63497, #65150 and #67820 edit `deepseek.rs` for other fixes and may need a rebase. #62812 changes only Python files, #62667's only Rust change is in `inkling/mod.rs`, and #66522 is a Python-only opt-in tokenize backend.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Enable VLM hidden states extraction
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Training a DFlash drafter for `nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse` requires capturing the target model’s hidden states on document images. Hidden-state extraction fails at startup for models that store their text config under `decoder`.

Based on the comments reply, I did an open PR search for `extract_hidden_states decoder` found no overlapping fix. [#38987](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38987) handled the conventional `text_config` key.

## Claims

- `extract_hidden_states` preserves the typed text config under its original Transformers key.
- Nemotron 3.5 Parse starts and exports hidden states for an expanded document prompt. Qwen3-VL exports the same token IDs and position-aligned hidden states for a two-image prompt under full and chunked prefill.

## Validation

The tested implementation and test sources match `c8aa02afb9fe84b2b720f4d4f3fb9ebd6fd4c514`. The baseline runs applied the current tests to the original PR base `2f170a0fed20fd84dfcf6da2a3a8188a32f67e4e`. Both configurations used the same Python 3.14, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, and Transformers 5.23.0 environment.

### Configuration regression

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states.py
```

On the PR base, Transformers rejected `decoder`, `generator`, and `text_encoder` when each appeared alongside an added `text_config`. The original `text_config` case passed.

```text
3 failed, 4 passed in 20.46s
```

With the fix, all four nested keys passed through `SpeculativeConfig` setup.

```text
7 passed in 18.61s
```

### VLM integration

Each run used one H100 with CUDA 13 and precompiled native artifacts from `0.34.0rc1.dev1014+g8586ccbcf`. The Nemotron Parse case uses `paper-11`. The Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct case uses `stop_sign` and `cherry_blossom` in the same request. Both cases check image placeholder expansion, exported prompt token IDs, and hidden-state shape. The Qwen3-VL case also compares the token IDs exactly and requires a cosine similarity of at least `0.999` for each token and layer across the two exports.

```bash
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
  uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -s --tb=short \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/extract_hidden_states_integration/test_extraction.py::test_extract_hidden_states_vision_language_model
```

On the PR base, Nemotron failed during startup and Qwen3-VL passed. The same Nemotron case run without the process wrapper for diagnosis surfaced `ValueError: Multiple valid text configs were found in the model config: ['decoder', 'text_config'].`

```text
1 failed, 1 passed, 2 warnings in 68.52s (0:01:08)
```

With the fix, both cases passed in the same pytest invocation.

```text
2 passed, 2 warnings in 92.09s (0:01:32)
```

#### Two-image prefill trace

For the same 1,468-token Qwen3-VL prompt, full prefill used one step. With a 1,024-token scheduling budget and `disable_chunked_mm_input=True`, the scheduler split the request between the two images. The exported token IDs and per-position hidden states passed the comparison.

The diagnostic run enabled iteration logging. The excerpts below omit timing and cache usage.

```text
Full prefill
Iteration(0): 1 context requests, 1468 context tokens ... encoder inputs: 2, encoder output embeddings: 1452

Chunked prefill
Iteration(0): 1 context requests, 732 context tokens ... encoder inputs: 1, encoder output embeddings: 726
Iteration(1): 1 context requests, 736 context tokens ... encoder inputs: 1, encoder output embeddings: 726
```

<details>
<summary>OpenAI server validation on a full page</summary>

The server validation applied the same extraction config patch to vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev975+g0d5306aac` on one H100.

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/vllm serve nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse \
  --served-model-name nemotron-parse --trust-remote-code \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18077 --enable-scale-out --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.18 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"extract_hidden_states","num_speculative_tokens":1,"draft_model_config":{"hf_config":{"eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids":[2,5,9,10]}}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"ExampleHiddenStatesConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"shared_storage_path":"/tmp/parse_hidden_states"}}'
```

The probe rendered one ParseBench page with `/v1/chat/completions/render` and submitted the same image and Parse task prompt to `/v1/chat/completions` with `kv_transfer_params.include_output_tokens=true`, `return_token_ids=true`, temperature 0, top-k 1, and max tokens 8,744. Both requests returned HTTP 200.

```text
prompt_tokens=2088
image_placeholder_tokens=2081
generated_tokens=1200
finish_reason=stop
aux_layer_ids=[2,5,9,10]
hidden_states_shape=[3287,4,1024]
hidden_states_dtype=torch.bfloat16
all_values_finite=true
token_ids_match=true
```

The match covers the rendered prompt and generated sequence through the penultimate generated token. The final sampled token has no forward pass and therefore has no exported row.

</details>

Pre-commit passed on all four changed files. The DCO sign-off hook passed for all three review commits.

## Details

`to_dict()` serializes typed Transformers sub-configs as dictionaries. On a Parse 3.5 target, the wrapper kept the serialized `decoder` and restored its typed value under `text_config`. Transformers sees both keys and raises at startup. The wrapper now restores the typed object under the original recognized key. Targets with a flat config or the conventional `text_config` key follow their prior paths.

The four keys come from `PreTrainedConfig.get_text_config()` in Transformers 5.23.0. Representative Hub configs include Qwen3-VL (`text_config`), Nemotron 3.5 Parse (`decoder`), Facebook RAG (`generator`), and MusicGen (`text_encoder`, selected with `encoder=True`). [Transformers source](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.23.0/src/transformers/configuration_utils.py) · [Qwen3-VL config](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct/blob/main/config.json) · [Nemotron config](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse/blob/main/config.json) · [RAG config](https://huggingface.co/facebook/rag-token-nq/blob/main/config.json) · [MusicGen config](https://huggingface.co/facebook/musicgen-small/blob/main/config.json)

The Nemotron and Qwen3-VL integration tests cover `decoder` and `text_config` end to end. Coverage for `generator` and `text_encoder` is currently limited to config-level regression tests.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used for the implementation, tests, and PR preparation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Match multimodal token counts to the processor for Unlimited-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR, MiniCPM-V 4.6 and MiniCPM-OCR
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Unlimited-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR, MiniCPM-V 4.6 and MiniCPM-OCR count multimodal tokens or apply processor options differently from their HF processors, so requests fail, budgets are too small, or startup profiles less encoder memory than a request needs. Follow-up from #67111; Unlimited-OCR follows #68127. ## Claims | Model | Main | This PR | |---|---|---| | Unlimited-OCR / -2 | A request-level `max_crops` below the default returns 500; with `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` the engine core dies | Placeholders read the processor's `num_image_tokens` | | DeepSeek-OCR / -2 | The square dummy tiles 2x2: budget 693 / 833, largest page 933 / 1,121 | Dummy is one column of `max_crops` tiles: 933 / 1,121 | | MiniCPM-V 4.6 | Image budget 648, real maximum 797 (an ordinary 1265x1112 image is 720); a 16-frame video is rejected at defaults; configured `max_slice_nums` and `downsample_mode` are ignored in profiling | Budgets 797 and 11,520 from 4.6's own token count; configured kwargs used | | MiniCPM-V 4.6 | The dummy is the input with the most tokens, but the encoder pads every slice to the widest one, so thin inputs need more encoder memory | Dummy chosen by padded input: video 184,320 -> 261,440 padded slots | | MiniCPM-V 4.6 | Admission allows one video up to the encoder budget (16,384 tokens at the H100/H200 offline and B200 defaults), but startup profiles 11,520: a 27-frame video runs out of memory on L4 | Profile sized by the encoder budget; the request is served | | MiniCPM-V 4.6 | `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0}` crashes at startup (vision tower marked image-only) | Vision tower loads for video-only | | MiniCPM-OCR | Video frames get upsize options no Transformers release has, so the engine fails to start at default limits; a scoped `small_image_upsize` is ignored | Frames pin `"always"`, images forward the option, budget 2,544 -> 2,858 | - Images above 200:1 and video frames above 50:1 are rejected for MiniCPM-V 4.6, 4.7 and MiniCPM-OCR, as other vLLM processors do for images; main accepted them past the budget. - At L4 default limits (FLASH_ATTN, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, same wheel), startup peak activation goes from 4.74 to 5.47 GiB and the KV cache from 1,127,095 to 1,065,269 tokens (-5.5%): startup now profiles the most padded video, and the 16-frame 1265x1112 video that main rejects is served. A 1265x1112 image gives identical greedy token ids. The image profile pass accounts for at most 0.01 GiB of that. Image-only MiniCPM-V 4.6 profiles 1.09 GiB more, for the 200:1 images main served unprofiled. ## Validation Each new test fails without its fix (transformers 5.23-5.24, CPU): ``` main ecc827ebbf E assert [2793] == [713] (Unlimited-OCR, max_crops 4) E assert 693 == 933 (DeepSeek-OCR) E assert 833 == 1121 (DeepSeek-OCR-2) E assert 648 == 797 (MiniCPM-V 4.6 image, 84x16726) E assert 10368 == (16 * 720) (MiniCPM-V 4.6 video) E Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError (MiniCPM-V 4.6, 201:1 image and 51:1 frame, x4) E assert 1440 == 144 (MiniCPM-V 4.6 video vs HF, max_slice_nums 1, x3) E TypeError: MiniCPMOcrImageProcessorKwargs.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'disable_small_image_upsize' (MiniCPM-OCR video, x4) E AssertionError: assert 252 == 28 (MiniCPM-OCR scoped small_image_upsize "never" vs HF, x2) 36 failed, 40 passed; this PR at fc2236892e: 76 passed 4b9ec641af (padded dummy) E AssertionError: assert 184320 >= 261440 (MiniCPM-V 4.6, 19-frame 7566x266 video vs the dummy) E assert (10 * 18928) >= (10 * 19152) (MiniCPM-OCR image dummy vs 126x14334, x3) 2af6ff8ec7 (encoder budget) E AssertionError: assert 261440 >= 371520 (max_num_batched_tokens 16384, 27-frame video vs profile) 19d893a897 (size hints, MiniCPM-OCR tiny images) E AssertionError: assert 184320 >= 371520 (video.width=8192, video.height=11000) E AssertionError: assert 11520 >= 18080 (image.width=8192, image.height=20000) E assert 28 >= 42 (MiniCPM-OCR scale_resolution 56, adaptive 196x1 image) 3340833bf4 (hints and the OCR budget) E AssertionError: assert 28 >= 42 (image hint 32x32 and 64x64) fe9d0bd65f (single-item profile, equal-token shapes) E AttributeError: 'MultiModalBudget' object has no attribute 'get_dummy_encoder_profile_single_input' (profile test, x6; before it, max_num_batched_tokens 24576 profiles 550,400 slots and a 41-frame 7566x266 video needs 564,160) E AssertionError: assert 8960 >= 9040 (max_slice_nums 4, image dummy vs 54x10800) 152801b3e0 (every slice count) E assert 36000 >= 38400 (8,192-token context, 4x video: dummy vs 8-frame 98x3796; 85x3363 and 3796x98 also fail) E assert 36000 >= 37632 (same, with a height=300, height=500 or width=8000,height=300 hint: 8-frame 3796x98) 092fc04dd3 (image batch next to 4x video) E AttributeError: 'MultiModalBudget' object has no attribute 'get_dummy_encoder_profile_modality_inputs' (image 1 / video 1, 4x video, 8,192 budget: profile 38,784 slots, six 20000x100 images 106,560, eight 142,080) E AssertionError: assert 153600 >= 157248 (image primary, video secondary: 39-frame 122x3284 video vs the dispatched passes, on the previous version of this commit) ``` All touched test files plus the encoder runner, warmup, EC connector and FlashInfer autotune tests at 092fc04dd3: 280 passed, 4 skipped on transformers 5.24.1; ## Details - **Unlimited-OCR.** The placeholder recomputed the count from the default `max_crops` while the processor used the request's value. It now reads `num_image_tokens` from the processor output, which also removes a copy of the multi-image crop rule. - **DeepSeek-OCR.** The dummy is `image_size` x `image_size * max_crops`, which always selects the 1 x `max_crops` layout, the one with the most tiles. - **MiniCPM-V 4.6 budget.** A search scores every slice grid with `max_slice_nums` or `max_slice_nums - 1` cells (1 to `max_slice_nums` for video frames) and slice heights within the aspect bound, using 4.6's own token count. It matches a brute-force maximum at 200:1 for `max_slice_nums` 1, 4, 9 and 16 in 16x and 4x, and is at or above it for 1 to 16 up to 8192x8192. The search looks up the image processor once and passes it to every candidate, as Qwen2-VL's `_get_vision_info` does, and scores each distinct size once. Building the image and video budgets takes 0.41 s per processor on CPU (0.79 s on fe9d0bd65f, which looked the processor up per candidate), and a startup builds three (input processor, scheduler, profiling run). With `max_slice_nums` 36 it takes 2.0 s (1.6 s on fe9d0bd65f). - **Padded dummy.** The dummy is the candidate with the most padded slots; a video dummy gets as many frames as its token budget allows. Among shapes with the same token count, the search keeps the one with the most padded slots (with `max_slice_nums=4` the image dummy moves from 12544x64 to 54x10800, 8,960 to 9,040 padded slots). Grids with fewer cells matter only for video, since smaller frames fit more of them in the budget (a 100,000-image scan per config finds nothing above the image dummy without them): with an 8,192-token context and 4x video the dummy moves from 3 frames of 7944x202 (36,000 slots) to 8 frames of 100x3976 (38,784), and a real 8-frame 98x3796 video needs 38,400. MiniCPM-V 4.6 at default settings and `max_model_len` 32768 keeps its dummy; at 8192 it moves from 178,880 to 181,632 slots, and MiniCPM-OCR's video dummy at 32768 from 151,840 to 156,816. The budget is unchanged, so the dummy can have fewer tokens than the budget (11,210 of 11,520). - **Encoder budget.** The scheduler runs one item up to `min(encoder compute budget, encoder cache size)`, which exceeds the per-item budget when `max_num_batched_tokens` is larger. Encoder profiling now asks the model for the context to fill through `get_dummy_seq_len(seq_len, max_encoder_tokens)`, a `BaseProcessingInfo` hook that returns `seq_len` by default, and passes each profiled item's share of the encoder budget. MiniCPM-V 4.6 fills it with frames. When the budget fits more than one item, the scheduler can also spend it on one video, so startup first runs a single dummy that fills the whole budget, then the split profile, and reserves for the higher peak (only when that dummy differs from the split one, which today means MiniCPM video). The hook is opt-in because models read `seq_len` in different units: passing the share to every model would shrink Ovis2.5's video dummy from 37,632 to 12,544 patches. `get_dummy_mm_inputs` gains an optional `seq_len`; GLM-5.3-Flash, the one in-tree override, accepts it too. - **Modalities.** Startup profiles the modality with the most tokens per item, but the scheduler can fill the encoder budget with another one, and MiniCPM pads every slice of a batch to its widest slice. With image 1 / video 1, 4x video and an 8,192-token budget, the video profile is 38,784 padded slots while six admitted 20000x100 images batch to 106,560 (main covered them only because it counts 4x video with 16x tokens). A `get_extra_profiled_modalities` hook on `BaseProcessingInfo`, empty by default, lists modalities whose batch profile startup also runs; MiniCPM-V 4.6 returns all of its modalities, so other models are unchanged. Each extra modality also gets the single full-budget pass when it differs from its split profile, and the primary batch still runs last: with image primary (4x images, `max_slice_nums` 16), 16x video with `max_slice_nums` 2 and `max_num_batched_tokens` 7810, the video split profile is 153,600 slots while an admitted 39-frame 122x3284 video needs 157,248, the size of the full-budget video dummy. - **Size hints.** If the unhinted dummy fits inside a width/height hint, it is used, since every input the hint allows is also allowed without it. Otherwise images keep main's dummy, or the largest accepted shape inside the hint when main's canvas is now rejected. Video takes whichever of main's dummy and the most padded shape inside the hint pads more once the dummy builder applies the hint, and the search inside the hint also scores each candidate's transpose. Hints never change the budget. - **MiniCPM-OCR.** Video frames pin `small_image_upsize="always"`, which the frame placeholder count assumes. `"always"` is the largest upsize mode when `scale_resolution` is at least 84; below that, `"adaptive"` upscales tiny unsliced images to 84 pixels, so the budget and dummy include that case (`scale_resolution` 56: 28 -> 42 tokens). The tiny-image constants are imported inside the methods because the MiniCPM-OCR processor exists only from Transformers 5.21, while vLLM supports 5.16.1. - **Tensor schema test.** It shrank images by truncating each side, which turned the 90x17804 (197.8:1) MiniCPM-V 4.6 dummy into 22x4451 (202.3:1), past the bound. It now keeps the aspect ratio. Of 68 image models checked on CPU, only MiniCPM-V 4.6, MiniCPM-OCR and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash get different shapes, and all three process. - **MiniCPM-V 4.7** reuses the 4.6 code. It was checked on CPU with `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B` and gives the same budgets and profiles. The test registry points it at `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4_7`, which is not public, so CI does not run it. Limits, unchanged from main unless stated: - For images, a hint that excludes the unhinted dummy can under-profile padding: with `image.height=500` startup profiles 3,072 padded slots per image, and a 20000x100 image needs 17,760. For video, a scan of 20,000 random videos inside the hint and the encoder budget, for each of 11 hints (width-only, height-only, combined, with `num_frames`) across 5 configs (MiniCPM-V 4.6 with one- and two-item budgets, 4x video at 8,192 and 32,768 contexts, MiniCPM-OCR), finds none above the profile; at `fe9d0bd65f` it found 37 of the 55 configs above it, up to 5.6x. - The image batch profile repeats the image dummy `encoder budget // most tokens per image` times, as main does. Images with fewer tokens fit more copies: at an 8,192-token budget with `max_num_seqs` 128, 18 admitted 76x15200 images (414 tokens each) batch to 260,352 padded slots against 180,800 profiled (main: 122,880 with 4x video, 138,240 image-only). A follow-up will choose the image dummy and its repeat count together. - The candidate search is not a proof. A 2M-shape random scan finds nothing larger at default settings. A scan of 100,000 random videos within the token budget per config (MiniCPM-V 4.6 default, 4x video, `max_slice_nums` 1 and 4, MiniCPM-OCR; 8,192 and 32,768 contexts) finds none above the dummy; before `152801b3e0` it found 110 (4x video) and 138 (MiniCPM-OCR) at 8,192, and 1 and 2 at 32,768, up to 7.7% above the dummy. - The encoder pads each scheduled batch to its widest slice, so one thin image (or video) batched with many small ones exceeds the profiled padded input: on L4, +2% encoder memory with FLASH_ATTN and +60% with TORCH_SDPA. - Videos above the encoder cache are rejected, as on main: a real 30 s 1080x1920 phone video, decoded by vLLM's loader at its default 32 frames, is 18,496 tokens. Real files through the loader were checked against the profile (640x360 at 32 and 64 frames, the 8K test asset, MiniCPM-V 4.6 and 4.7-1B): every admitted one fits. With 2 and 4 videos per prompt, an encoder step filled with same-shape or mixed-shape videos also fits (worst 357,760 of 371,520 padded slots at 16384).
Same check on other models (CPU) `max_model_len` 32768, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, raw frame arrays from 640x360 to 1920x1080 and up to 384 frames, largest admitted single video vs everything startup profiles: - Clean: Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3.5, InternS1-Pro, Cosmos3 and the Transformers backend cap a video at their 12,288-token budget; GLM-OCR at its dummy. LLaVA-OneVision (5 x 3,137 profiled, largest 12,545) and Muse-Glimmer (2 x 6,912, largest 13,824) are covered by their profiled items. - Above the profile: JinaVL (3 x 5,376, largest 16,384) and Gemma 4 (6 x 2,048, largest 16,384; #67112 changes its dummy) by less than one item. Ovis2.5 (2 x 6,274, 8 frames of 1920x1080 is 16,322) has a different bug: its video budget undercounts HD video. Their encoder memory isn't measured, so they are left out of this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor reasoning_effort and documents in /tokenize
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/tokenize` ignores `reasoning_effort` and `documents`, so for the same body it returns a different prompt than `/v1/chat/completions` renders. This affects both the Python and the Rust frontend.

- Python: `TokenizeChatRequest.build_chat_params` only forwarded `add_generation_prompt` and `continue_final_message`, and the other two fields were silently dropped because the request model accepts extra keys.
- Rust: the tokenize request lowered the body into a chat request with `reasoning_effort` and `documents` hard-coded to `None`.

## Claims

- `/tokenize` returns the same prompt token ids as the chat route for requests with `reasoning_effort` (including its `enable_thinking` mapping and `--reasoning-effort-map`) and `documents`, on both frontends.
- Requests without these fields render exactly as before.

## Validation

Reproducer (RTX 3090, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `vllm serve --trust-request-chat-template`): POST the same body to `/tokenize` and to `/v1/chat/completions` with `max_tokens=1, return_token_ids=true`, then compare the ids.

| Body | `/tokenize` before | chat prompt | `/tokenize` after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reasoning_effort: "none"` | 15 tokens, ends with `<\|im_start\|>assistant\n` | 19 tokens, ends with `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` | 19, identical |
| `documents` + a template that renders them | 12 tokens, documents missing | 24 tokens, `[DOC Math: 2+2 equals 4.]...` | 24, identical |

The Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) shows the same numbers before and after, including `reasoning_effort: "minimal"` with `--reasoning-effort-map '{"minimal":"none"}'` (15 vs 19 before, 19 vs 19 after).

This matters for clients that use `/tokenize` to count tokens or to build prompt ids for token-in/token-out generation: they get a prompt the server would not generate from.

New tests, run first without the source changes and then with them:


commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] WRITE mode free prefill blocks released during prefill or under reused transfer id
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In MoRIIO WRITE mode, the prefill instance can hold a finished request's KV blocks until it restarts, either because the decode instance released the transfer while the prompt was still being prefilled or because the request reused the transfer id of an earlier request. This PR makes sure every such request still gets the completion report that frees its blocks.



## Claims

- A WRITE request that decode released early, or that reuses an ended transfer id, frees its prefill blocks as soon as it finishes.
- Experimented on MI355X with Qwen3-0.6B, all 32 requests released during their prefill stayed allocated on main, and none did with this PR. The same holds for 8 requests that reused an ended transfer id.
- Serving accuracy does not change. With Qwen3-4B on the full GSM8K test set, WRITE mode scores 0.872 / 0.867 (strict-match / flexible-extract) on main and 0.876 / 0.867 with this PR, and READ mode scores 0.879 / 0.875 and 0.874 / 0.872, against 0.878 / 0.873 without a connector.
- An early release for a request that ended without holding blocks, such as an aborted prefill, still expires after `defer_timeout` as it does on main.



## Validation

### Unit tests

The new tests are in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_write_done_routing.py`. They run the real `Scheduler` with the MoRIIO producer through `schedule` and `update_from_output`, and one worker rank through `start_load_kv`, `wait_for_save` and `get_finished` with the real `MoRIIOWriter` and `MoRIIOWrapper`. Release messages enter through `MoRIIOWrapper._handle_structured_message`, and the scheduler runs on a fake clock. Reverting any one part of the change makes its tests fail.

| Scenario | Tests | Main | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| A release that arrives during a 4-chunk prefill frees the request when it finishes, ten `defer_timeout` periods later | `test_decode_release_during_a_long_prefill_frees_its_blocks_when_it_finishes` | 1 failed (held) | 1 passed |
| A queued request whose release was buffered and then dropped unmatched is freed when it finishes | `test_queued_request_frees_its_blocks_when_its_unmatched_release_was_dropped` | 1 failed (held) | 1 passed |
| A request that reuses the transfer id of an ended request, scheduled right after the first one was freed, is freed when it finishes | `test_request_reusing_an_ended_transfer_id_frees_its_blocks_when_it_finishes` (2 cases) | 2 failed (held) | 2 passed |
| A release of a transfer with queued or deferred writes leaves no writer state behind | `test_release_of_a_transfer_with_scheduled_writes_leaves_no_writer_state` (2 cases) | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| A parked release of an aborted prefill still expires after `defer_timeout` | `test_parked_ack_of_an_aborted_prefill_is_dropped_after_the_defer_timeout` | 1 passed | 1 passed |

### End-to-end verification

Prefill and decode each run on one MI355X GPU connected by MoRIIO WRITE over xGMI. Both use ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN with PIECEWISE CUDA graphs and async scheduling.

The leak runs use Qwen3-0.6B with a test copy of the example moriio proxy. For long requests it runs only the prefill leg and sends the prefill instance the `release` message that decode sends when it drops a request before scheduling it. Short requests, such as the readiness probe and the warm-up, take the normal path.

- **Release during the prefill.** 32 requests of 16,384 random tokens are sent 8 at a time, and each is released right after its prefill leg is sent. The prefill instance runs with a `defer_timeout` of 0.25 s, `--max-num-batched-tokens 64` and no prefix caching, so each prefill computes for 1.40 to 1.48 s and every release arrives at least 2.0 s before its prefill returns.
- **Reused transfer ids.** 8 pairs of 4,096-token requests are sent one at a time, and both requests of a pair share a transfer id. The first request of each pair is released either when it is sent, before any write, or after it returns, while its writes wait for decode. The second is sent 2 s after the first returns, while the prefill instance is idle, and is never released.

| Scenario | Measure | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Released during the prefill | Requests completed, errors | 32, 0 | 32, 0 |
| | Requests still allocated after the load | 32 | 0 |
| | Prefill KV cache usage after the load | 21.3% for 62 s | 0.0% |
| Reused ids, released before the writes | Requests completed, errors | 16, 0 | 16, 0 |
| | Requests still allocated, prefill KV cache usage | 8, 1.4% | 0, 0.0% |
| Reused ids, released while the writes wait | Requests completed, errors | 16, 0 | 16, 0 |
| | Requests still allocated, prefill KV cache usage | 8, 1.4% | 0, 0.0% |
| | `MoRIIOWriter` entries left per map | 8 | 0 |

"Still allocated" counts the entries in `MoRIIOConnectorScheduler._deferred_send_deadlines`, sampled every 10 s by a test-only hook. After the first load on main, the prefill instance logs `Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 21.3%`. In the reused-id runs, the 8 requests held on main are the second request of each pair, whose writes are refused because the id is in the record of ended transfers.

The serving check uses Qwen3-4B with the same flags and the unmodified toy proxy, in both WRITE and READ mode. The READ runs use TRITON_ATTN with FULL CUDA graphs, no async scheduling and a 2 s `transfer_timeout`. GSM8K covers the full test set of 1,319 questions, 5-shot with 64 concurrent requests. Cells show strict-match / flexible-extract, and the baseline is the same model without a connector at TP1.

| Mode | Main | This PR | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| WRITE | 0.872 / 0.867 | 0.876 / 0.867 | 0.878 / 0.873 |
| READ | 0.879 / 0.875 | 0.874 / 0.872 | 0.878 / 0.873 |

<details>
<summary>commands</summary>

Each vLLM instance runs in its own container (vLLM ROCm image at cf5cea2da3 with MoRI v1.2.3.post1, plus this branch for the PR runs). The proxy, the load and `lm_eval` run in a third container without `--pid=host` and the device flags.

```bash
docker run -d --network=host --ipc=host --pid=host --group-add=video \
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE --cap-add=IPC_LOCK --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --device /dev/infiniband \
  --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 \
  -v $HF_HOME:/root/.cache/huggingface <image> sleep infinity

HOST_IP=<node IP>
P_KV='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8100", "handshake_port": "8104", "notify_port": "8120", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi"}}'
D_KV='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8200", "handshake_port": "8204", "notify_port": "8220", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi"}}'
# release during the prefill: P only, with "defer_timeout": 0.25 added
P_KV_SHORT='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8100", "handshake_port": "8104", "notify_port": "8120", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi", "defer_timeout": 0.25}}'
# READ: "read_mode": true, "transfer_timeout": 2 added on both
P_KV_READ='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8100", "handshake_port": "8104", "notify_port": "8120", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi", "read_mode": true, "transfer_timeout": 2}}'
D_KV_READ='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8200", "handshake_port": "8204", "notify_port": "8220", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi", "read_mode": true, "transfer_timeout": 2}}'

# P on GPU 0 and D on GPU 1. Each instance lists the other's GPU after its own,
# so that MoRI can reach the peer's memory over xGMI.
WRITE='--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"} --async-scheduling'
# release during the prefill
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8100 $WRITE --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 64 --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV_SHORT"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8200 $WRITE --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"
# reused transfer ids
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8100 $WRITE --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8200 $WRITE --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"
# serving, WRITE
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --port 8100 $WRITE --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --port 8200 $WRITE --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"
# serving, READ
READ='--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"} --no-async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching'
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --port 8100 $READ --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV_READ"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --port 8200 $READ --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV_READ"
# baseline, without a connector
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --port 8300 --tensor-parallel-size 1

# proxy: the toy proxy for serving, its test copy for the leak runs
python3 examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 8001
python3 moriio_toy_proxy_release.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 8001 --release-min-tokens 4096 --release-when dispatch
python3 moriio_toy_proxy_release.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 8001 --release-min-tokens 2048 --release-when dispatch --reuse-transfer-ids --reuse-delay-s 2
python3 moriio_toy_proxy_release.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 8001 --release-min-tokens 2048 --release-when response --reuse-transfer-ids --reuse-delay-s 2
# The test copy sends msgpack.dumps({"type": "release", "transfer_id": <id>, "consumer_tp_size": 1})
# on a ZMQ DEALER socket to notify_port + get_port_offset(dp_rank, tp_rank) of every P rank.

# leak load: 32 prompts of 16,384 random token ids (1000-100000), 8 at a time, or 16 prompts of 4,096, one at a time
curl -s http://$HOST_IP:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "prompt": [<token ids>], "max_tokens": 2, "temperature": 0}'
# P's KV cache usage, every 2 s for 60 s after the last request returned
curl -s http://$HOST_IP:8100/metrics | grep '^vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc'

# GSM8K on all 1,319 questions, with PORT=8000 (the proxy) for P/D and 8300 for the baseline
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 0 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3-4B,base_url=http://$HOST_IP:$PORT/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=1,tokenized_requests=False,timeout=3600

pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -k moriio
```

</details>



## Details

In WRITE mode the prefill scheduler keeps a finished request's blocks in `_deferred_send_deadlines` until the worker reports the transfer done through `finished_sending`. The hold has no timeout on purpose, because only the worker knows when no write can still read the blocks. The worker sends that report when the writes complete, fail or time out, or when a release from decode ends the transfer. On main the report can be lost in three ways.

- An early report is parked in `_pending_sent_acks`, and `MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.update_connector_output` drops it `defer_timeout` later whether or not the request has finished. Decode releases a transfer it never allocated when it aborts the request before scheduling it or has nothing left to fetch, and with a proxy that starts both legs at once that release can reach the prefill instance while the prompt is still being prefilled. By the time the report is dropped the transfer is already final, so every write is refused and no second report ever comes.
- The wrapper remembers the ids of the last 4,096 ended transfers, and `MoRIIOWriter.schedule_write` refuses every write of a request that reuses one of them. This happens, for example, when a router derives the transfer id from a client request id and the client retries. Since nothing is queued, nothing reports. The worker also prunes its record of acknowledged transfers only once an id is no longer mapped, so on an otherwise idle prefill instance the reusing request's own report would be dropped as a duplicate.
- When a release ends a transfer whose writes are queued or still waiting for decode's allocation, `_write_worker_loop` and `_process_deferred_tasks` drop the tasks without calling `_clear_transfer_state`. The writer then keeps `_scheduled_writes`, `_scheduled_layers` and `_sealed_writes` for that transfer, which also hides a later reuse of the id.

The leak runs reproduce each case. A 16,384-token prompt at a 64-token batch budget keeps the prefill busy for about 1.4 s, well past the 0.25 s `defer_timeout`, and in the reused-id pairs the second request arrives after the first one's transfer has ended.

The fix closes each of these paths and ties the worker's duplicate check to the request that owns the id:
- `MoRIIOConnectorScheduler._unfinished_write_sends` tracks WRITE producer requests from `update_state_after_alloc` until `request_finished`. `update_connector_output` expires a parked report only for requests outside that set, so an early release frees its request as soon as the request finishes. Reports for requests that ended without holding blocks expire as on main.
- `MoRIIOWriter.ack_refused_transfers` runs in `wait_for_save` before `seal_pending_transfers` and reports every transfer in the step's `reqs_to_save` that is final and has no scheduled write. None of that request's writes were queued, so freeing its blocks is safe. If decode already released the transfer, the report is a duplicate, and `resolve_moriio_transfer_ack` drops it while the transfer is still mapped.
- The write worker and the deferred loop call `_clear_transfer_state` when they drop a task of a final transfer, as finalize and the allocation timeout already do.
- `MoRIIOConnectorWorker._completed_notification_owners` records which request each report was resolved for, and `start_load_kv` keeps a transfer in `_completed_consumer_notifications` only while that request still owns the id.

Cases where two live requests that share one transfer id are not covered here. The prefill instance also still sends nothing to decode for a refused transfer, because decode may have mapped that id to another live request, so decode's side of a reused id waits for its own receive deadline.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix `test_ihc_shards_rows_and_preserves_generation[True]` in `tests/models/hy_v4/test_sequence_parallel.py` on ROCm. It fails on main in `(MI355) HY4 Distributed` with `AttributeError: 'HYV4DecoderLayer' object has no attribute 'ihc_attn_boundary'` ([ci build 106166](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/106166/list?jid=01a21bd1-87b1-42b6-ae45-c3de6c7d3af2&tab=output)).

## Claims

The test passes on MI355X again. The NVIDIA path is unchanged: the hook is still registered on the fused boundary when the layer has one.

## Validation

On MI355X (gfx950), 2 GPUs, commit 0ed20f2515, from `tests/`:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v -s models/hy_v4/test_sequence_parallel.py
```

Before:

```
FAILED models/hy_v4/test_sequence_parallel.py::test_ihc_shards_rows_and_preserves_generation[True] - Exception: Call to collective_rpc method failed: Worker failed with error ''HYV4DecoderLayer' object has no attribute 'ihc_attn_boundary''
1 failed, 18 warnings in 42.52s
```

After:

```
2 passed, 23 warnings in 183.56s (0:03:03)
```

The test asserts that rows with at least 1024 tokens were observed, so a pass also confirms the hooks fired on the ROCm layer.

## Details

#69780 moved the row check hooks to `layer.ihc_attn_boundary` and `layer.ihc_mlp_boundary`, which only the NVIDIA decoder layer (`vllm/models/hy_v4/nvidia/model.py`) defines. #70004 then enabled this test on ROCm, where `vllm/models/hy_v4/amd/model.py` has no such attributes. Only the `enforce_eager=True` case installs the hooks, so `[False]` still passed.

The test now reads the boundaries with `getattr(..., None)`, so on ROCm it falls back to `hc_pre`, as before #69780. The model code is not changed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][UMBP] Restore Mamba hybrid prefixes at boundaries inside attention blocks
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A Mamba hybrid that checkpoints its state inside an attention block never restores from UMBP at that checkpoint, so a returning prompt resumes from an older boundary or is computed again.

Store the attention page with each state page core hands off at such a boundary, keyed at the same boundary, as the finished-tail path already does.
Default `enable_partial_hash_hits` to true for Mamba hybrids whose `prefix_match_unit` is finer than the scheduler block, since only hash-granular lookups reach those checkpoints. An explicit setting still wins, and other models keep `false`.

The fix adds the pages to the entries `_add_boundary_state_plans` already turns into store plans, so plan construction and its checks stay in one place. It reads each page from core's current block table (`KVConnectorBlockState.get_block_ids`), which also covers `lazy_offload`, whose request tracker does not grow with the table. The default is a separate commit and is documented in `docs/features/umbp_store_connector_usage.md`.

```bash
pytest -v -s -rs tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_hybrid.py -k "restores_every_byte or partial_hash_hits_default or boundary_page_comes_from"
pytest -v -s -rs tests/v1/kv_connector/umbp_integration/test_mori_token_e2e.py -k hybrid
```

Commits: `5f79879241` (fix), `913429afc0` (default) and `813c7461d7` (the page from core's current table, for `lazy_offload`), on main `9e8b3fb83e`.

## Claims

- A Mamba hybrid restores from UMBP at the same boundary as a local GPU prefix hit, with identical tokens and logprobs. Granite 4.0-H 350M: 0 → 832 restored tokens of an 840-token prompt.
- Nemotron-H-8B keeps its GSM8K accuracy with 98.8% of the prompt tokens restored from UMBP.
- Kimi-K3.1-Pro on one MI355X node: 13,910 → 16,824 tok/s/GPU (+21%), prefix hit 90.7% → 94.1%, TTFT p90 5.45 → 3.03 s.

## Validation

Before the rebase onto main: one MI355X node, vLLM nightly `9bc16ae6a3` (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-9bc16ae6a34b1e0fe260e8d12b98568478bf38c3`, MORI v1.2.3.post1) with the test requirements installed as in the CI image, on `b0d03d9e22`.

- UMBP unit tests: 386 passed. Without the fix, `test_hybrid_boundary_restores_every_byte[running-cpu]` and `[running-cuda]` fail with `assert 1 == 2`, since only the state page is stored; their `finished` cases pass on main too. Without the default, `test_partial_hash_hits_default_on_for_mamba_hybrids[True-4-None-True]` fails.
- UMBP integration on one GPU: 20 passed, 2 skipped (they need 2 GPUs). The TP2 step passes both. `test_hybrid_restores_a_boundary_inside_an_attention_block` runs in embedded and standalone mode, and both fail on main with `assert (0 - 0) == ((2 * 400) + 32)`. It runs Granite 4.0-H 350M with `prefix_match_unit=16` (400-token blocks), so an 840-token prompt checkpoints at 832, then resets the GPU prefix cache, restores the prompt from UMBP and compares tokens and logprobs with a local prefix hit. It sets `enable_partial_hash_hits` explicitly, so it tests the fix alone.
- Pre-commit passes on the changed files (mypy in a Python 3.12 container).

On main `9e8b3fb83e` (after #63830, #66234 and #63002), vLLM nightly `c2cc003c5b`, 13 commits before it and with no UMBP changes in between (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-c2cc003c5b644095cabcd5212d2967546ce344f8`, Python 3.14), one MI355X node, on `813c7461d7`:

Before `813c7461d7`, `pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_hybrid.py -k boundary_page_comes_from` gave `1 failed, 1 passed, 60 deselected, 17 warnings in 1.02s`: with `lazy_offload` only the state was stored (`assert {(0, 2), (1, 6)} <= {(1, 6)}`).

|---|---:|---|---:|---|

<summary>Kimi-K3.1 server command (the same in every run apart from the KV transfer config)</summary>

```
vllm serve /model \

  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 --load-format fastsafetensors --gpu-memory-utilization 0.91 \
  --language-model-only --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --stream-interval 10 --seed 7 --max-num-seqs 48 --max-num-batched-tokens 10240 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":10240,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"/data/Kimi-K3.1-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":2.7}' \
  --additional-config '{"kda_prefill_backend":"fused"}' \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"dsa_config":{"indexer_use_fp8":true}}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"UMBPStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mode":"embedded","capacity_bytes":322122547200,"enable_partial_hash_hits":true,"dram_use_hugepages":true,"dram_hugepage_size":2097152,"dram_numa_node":-1,"dram_prefault":true}}'
```

`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` runs use `{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":322122547200,"lazy_offload":false}}`. The CUDA graph capture sizes (4 to 10240) and the ROCm/AITER environment are the recipe's and are omitted here. The client replays an agentic coding trace with AIPerf at concurrency 48 for 3600 s after a 300 s warmup; tok/s/GPU is (input + output) throughput / 8.
</details>

## Details

Turn 1 computes its prompt, and core checkpoints the Mamba state at the prompt-tail boundary `b`, inside attention block `k`, and hands that state page to UMBP. UMBP stored attention blocks `0..k-1` and the state, but not block `k`, which holds tokens `[k*B, b)`. On the next turn, after the GPU cache dropped turn 1, the lookup coordinator needs every group to hit at the same boundary: Mamba hits at `b` and attention stops at `k*B`, so it settles on an older boundary where both hit, if any. With this PR block `k` is stored too, keyed at `b`, and the turn resumes at `b`.

The first version of this fix, written for Kimi-K3 in charxwu/vllm#19 on October 15, also keyed the page for EAGLE block drop, which DSpark used then. Block drop now applies only with `disable_lookahead_block_hashes`, where lookups match attention one unit past a boundary and do not use these pages, so this PR leaves that case as it is; vllm-project/vllm#66234 removes the drop.

Cost: one more attention page per handed-off checkpoint; on Kimi-K3.1 that page is about a third of the size of the KDA checkpoint it goes with. With the default, hybrid lookups probe one key per prefix-match unit instead of per block, which #67943 makes cheaper.

Limitation, unchanged by this PR: a lookup does not pin what it finds, so a pool that evicts quickly can drop a hit before its load, and under the default `kv_load_failure_policy=fail` that request fails. Hybrids now reach this path. With the 4 GiB pool `test_gsm8k_offloading.py` gives UMBP, Nemotron-H-8B writes about 25 GB of KV per GSM8K pass; a restored pass had 28 failed loads and 4 of 200 requests failed. `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute` recomputed those loads, and a 64 GiB pool had none.

Related: vllm-project/vllm#63670 (exploratory draft) adds the same pages in `_add_boundary_state_plans` while it removes the align-mode prefill chunk split and `register_finished_partial_tail`. This PR is the standalone fix on current main: it takes the block table from UMBP's request tracker, so it needs no core change, and it keeps the finished-tail path. No other open PR changes this path or this default.

commits.pr_title: [CI][XPU] Re-enable KV and EC connector tests in Intel GPU CI
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This change follows the CUDA CI approach in [vllm-project/vllm#65145](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65145) for hash-locked XPU KV connector dependencies, re-enabling Intel XPU KV connector coverage and aligning Intel V1 job separation with CUDA.

## Claims



- Add a dedicated hash-locked dependency set for XPU KV connector tests, including `lmcache==0.5.7.post1`.
- Re-enable Intel V1 tests and add/split CI jobs for V1 Core, KV + EC connectors, EC CPU, Metrics, and NIXL integration coverage.
- Run the Qwen3-30B KV connector job on a two-GPU K8s resource; remove its runtime `pip install dpctl`.
- Exclude `cuda-bindings` from the XPU KV lock to avoid loading CUDA 13 Python bindings in the XPU environment.

## Validation



- XPU dependency lock pins and hashes reproduce successfully.
- Buildkite YAML parsing and job dependency checks pass.

| label | agent | Runtime in CI | estimated frequency (post-merge) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| :intel: (BMG) V1 Core | 1xB50 | 7min05s | 7.7 times/day |
| :intel: (BMG) V1 KV + EC Connectors | 1xB50 | 13min53s | 2 times/day |
| :intel: (BMG) EC CPU Connector | 1xB70 | 1min47s | 12.0 times/day |
| :intel: (BMG) V1 Metrics + LM Eval | 1xB50 | 2min05s | 10.6 times/day |
| :intel: (BMG) V1 test | 1xB50 | 10 min | 13 times/day |
| :intel: (BMG) Qwen3-30B + V1 KV Connector | 2xB70 | 10min50s | 13 times/day |

## Details



Previously disabled Intel jobs installed `dpctl` at runtime. The XPU image now installs KV connector dependencies from a separate hash-locked requirements file, and the jobs use the image-provided packages.

in registry?"} A -->|Hit| B["Reuse base"] A -->|Miss on main CI| C["Build and publish base"] A -->|Miss on premerge CI| D["Build the whole image
(the same as previous)"] B --> E["Bake image using base"] C --> E D --> F["Push per-commit image"] E --> F ``` ## Validation ### To reproduce "image build, publish, and reuse" locally ```bash docker run -d --name xpu-e2e-registry -p 127.0.0.1:5009:5000 registry:2 REGISTRY=127.0.0.1:5009 REPO="xpu-e2e-$(date +%s)" # PR miss: build the whole image BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST=42 BUILDKITE_BRANCH=feature \ bash .buildkite/image_build/image_build_xpu.sh "$REGISTRY" "$REPO" pr-miss # main miss: build and publish base image, then continue building the whole image BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST=false BUILDKITE_BRANCH=main \ bash .buildkite/image_build/image_build_xpu.sh "$REGISTRY" "$REPO" main-miss # PR hit: reuse published base image, and continue building the whole image BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST=42 BUILDKITE_BRANCH=feature \ bash .buildkite/image_build/image_build_xpu.sh "$REGISTRY" "$REPO" pr-hit ``` condensed result: ``` # for case 1: PR miss XPU base image not found; building from the Dockerfile ··· pr-miss-xpu: digest: sha256:b1f1ec52b337c4dd3afffd60353072d67bc476dd1fef1458bf88759525d17141 size: 856 # case 2: main miss Building and publishing 127.0.0.1:5009/xpu-e2e-1795149764:xpu-base-55e033bf3e8f8620d3f3e8dd2d41fa70 ··· Published 127.0.0.1:5009/xpu-e2e-1795149764:xpu-base-55e033bf3e8f8620d3f3e8dd2d41fa70@sha256:26f9655dd43750fdcc554932b46f839e459fc1e1ee366f894a0458d3e82282da ··· main-miss-xpu: digest: sha256:93d0b1f7a13c5cb3bb4934800d74e437777c9451f7d56776d7d3a433d990fe20 size: 856 # case 3: PR hit XPU base image found: 127.0.0.1:5009/xpu-e2e-1795149764:xpu-base-55e033bf3e8f8620d3f3e8dd2d41fa70@sha256:26f9655dd43750fdcc554932b46f839e459fc1e1ee366f894a0458d3e82282da ··· pr-hit-xpu: digest: sha256:8b402dd0d07221ea9668991d2dac7df48b44241703e8aaa90b4348aba8838ae6 size: 856 ``` ### new UT for virtual test: ``` pytest -q tests/tools/test_xpu_image_build.py ``` result: passed `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed ## Details what's changed: - XPU dockerfile and image building script. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Skip unused embedding packs and refresh tied LM heads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

CPU vocabulary embeddings build a GEMM weight pack even though token lookup uses the original weight. A tied LM head can also keep its old pack after a checkpoint reload updates the shared embedding. Skip the lookup-only pack and prepare the head after the shared weights have finished loading.

## Claims

- Qwen2.5-0.5B uses one fewer oneDNN weight buffer, saving 272,269,312 bytes (259.66 MiB).
- The tied LM head uses the updated vocabulary after a layerwise reload or an in-place kernel-format update of the shared vocabulary tensor.

## Validation

Linux arm64 validation on `69f420d614`: the existing weight-tying and direct-reload suites passed (`54 passed in 8.91s`). Both standalone Qwen reload checks (checkpoint and kernel format) also passed with a spawned worker on that source (`2 passed in 23.11s`). The regression cases used during development are available in [2cc3fc2efc](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/2cc3fc2efc9014bc79083c7c628e99fc6b92e82d).

Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B in BF16 on a Linux arm64 VM with four CPU threads, TP=1, a 256 MiB KV cache, and eager execution. The comparison uses main at `1489434bd5` and that source with this patch. The CPU kernels came from wheel commit `9bc16ae6a3`, which has the same CPU kernel sources and build settings. The file I/O extension was rebuilt from the test base.

| Check | Main | With this change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Resident oneDNN weight buffers | 98 | 97 |
| Bytes in those buffers | 1,260,191,744 | 987,922,432 |
| LM head maximum absolute difference from a fresh pack after negating the shared weights | 2.109375 | 0 |

Across nine fixed workloads totaling 39 requests, all 624 generated token IDs and 3,120 returned top-5 logprob values matched. The layerwise and kernel-format vocabulary updates both matched a fresh pack. Restoring the original weights restored the exact tokens and logprobs. The buffer count stayed at 97 after each of the four updates.

<details>
<summary>Regression commands and output</summary>

The following historical commands use the [layer tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2cc3fc2efc9014bc79083c7c628e99fc6b92e82d/tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py) and [real-model test](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2cc3fc2efc9014bc79083c7c628e99fc6b92e82d/tests/models/language/generation/test_cpu_embedding_prepack.py) from the earlier PR revision. To rerun them as written, check out `2cc3fc2efc`, which has the same production fix.

```sh
OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py -k cpu_embedding -q --tb=short

OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-3 \
  VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
  VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_cpu_embedding_prepack.py -q --tb=short
```

On main, the layer cases fail on the unused pack or the missing `cpu_linear` on the standalone projection path. The real model case fails on the unused embedding pack.

```text
    assert getattr(embedding, "cpu_linear", None) is None
E   AssertionError: assert <function dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm.<locals>.<lambda> ...> is None
6 failed, 4 deselected
1 failed
```

Both commands pass on the patched source.

```text
6 passed, 4 deselected
1 passed
```

The initial validation passed all 10 cases in the weight tying test file. The real model case passed in process and with a spawned worker. Each generation phase uses one request to keep batch shape fixed. Pre-commit passed for all changed files.

</details>

November 18 combined layer/reload check on the merged source:

```sh
OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_direct_reload.py -q --tb=short
# 55 passed in 10.36s
```

## Details

On a layerwise checkpoint reload, the loader restores the tied parameter on the LM head when it has no checkpoint entry of its own. It skips that head's quant method processing, which previously left the old GEMM pack in use. Kernel-format reload already runs the common model finalizer after copying weights. Preparing the head in that finalizer covers both paths. An embedding used directly as a logits projector prepares GEMM on its first projection, which is where that path now pays its initial packing cost.

Public issue and open PR searches for embedding prepack and CPU reload found no other change targeting this pack lifecycle. The related work covers re-tying during direct reload and a general contract for refreshing derived state. [#66487](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66487) · [#60931](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60931)

## Overview

Adds three GB200 presets to the Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe for the vLLM AgentX lanes of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#5199](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5199), pinned to the image the lanes ran, `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-arm64-cu135-7074371@sha256:4fc725bb…`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds GB200 to this recipe. The open Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe PRs (#65865, #65958, #66635, #70188) cover Zhenwu, MI325X, MI355X and B300.

## Claims

- `gb200_agentx_tp16` (Multi-Node TP): one aggregated TP16 + DCP16 engine on four trays with the low-latency decode backend, at 1, 4 and 8 clients.
- `gb200_agentx_pd_tp16` (PD, vLLM Router, NIXL): one TP16 + DCP16 prefill worker with EP16 on MegaMoE and one TP16 + DCP16 decode worker, at 32 and 64 clients.
- `gb200_agentx_pd_pp2` (PD, vLLM Router, pushed NIXL): one TP8 x PP2 prefill worker and one decode worker of two or four TP8 data-parallel ranks, at 140, 160, 170, 200 and 210 clients.
- GB200 joins the recipe's hardware, with DCP sizes 8 and 16 and a 16-GPU floor (two trays, 1536 GB, are short of the 1561 GB checkpoint).

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` from vllm-project/recipes main passes.
- For all 10 points, the rendered `vllm serve` args and env of every role equal the InferenceX#5199 recipe blocks merged with their base (`agg-tp16-variants.yaml`, `disagg-tp16-dcp16-variants.yaml`, `disagg-p-tp8pp2-variants.yaml`), apart from the benchmark-only settings each runbook lists.
- InferenceX#5199's sweep passed on this configuration, all 10 points: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/45560044986 (GSM8K strict match 0.979 to 0.983 on the five evaluated rows).

## Details

- The image is a branch build; the TP8 x PP2 prefill layout, `NixlPushConnector` across pipeline stages and `VLLM_DP_SESSION_AFFINITY_*` exist only in it, as the runbook says.
- The builder has no connector entry for `NixlPushConnector`, so `gb200_agentx_pd_pp2` leaves `select.pd_connector` unset and renames the default NIXL connector with `json_args`.
- The builder renders `vllm-router --policy round_robin`; the lane's `consistent_hash` policy, request timeout and `--disable-retries` are in the runbooks.
- The presets keep the lane's `--gpu-memory-utilization` values, as the other AgentX presets of this recipe do.
- `gb200: verified` rests on these presets; the baseline GB200 command on the default image was not run.

commits.pr_title: [Model][Hardware] Inkling: relative attention on SM8x via Inkling 2's Triton kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#69165 runs Inkling 2 on Ampere/Ada (SM80/86/89). Inkling (v1) still fails there: its FA4 score_mod attention raises `NotImplementedError` below SM90.

This PR makes Inkling (v1) attention work on SM8x. On SM8x it shears the relative logits into the `(T + 128, H, E + 256)` layout of Inkling 2's paged Triton `rel_attention` kernel, which #69165 runs on SM8x, and uses that kernel for prefill, decode and sliding-window layers.

- **No new kernel.** Ampere/Ada share one Triton kernel across both Inkling generations.
- **CUDA-graph safe.** The shear has static shapes and no host sync.
- **No FA4 warmup on SM8x.** The FA4 JIT warmup is skipped there, since that kernel never runs.
- **Tests:** the kernel tests in `tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_rel_attention.py` now also run on SM80+. The FA4-only score_mod test stays SM90+.

Recipe changes are left out of this PR, per review. The validation below also covers Inkling 2 Small on A100 (multi-node TP8), which needs no code beyond #69165.

## Validation

### Inkling (v1), the change in this PR

Inkling-Small-NVFP4 (b6a99534), one node, 4x A100-SXM4-80GB, TP4, torch 2.14.0+cu130 (precompiled extensions):
- `pytest tests/models/inkling -q -rs`: `216 passed, 51 skipped in 158.18s (0:02:38)`. The skips are ROCm-only and Hopper-only tests.
- **Attention parity** against an fp32 reference on 10 shapes, all passing: prefill, 4K global prefill, a 2K chunk on 3K context, decode, global and sliding-window layers, and mixed batches.
- **`vllm serve` end to end** with `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 65536`, the tool-call and reasoning parsers, the V2 model runner and CUDA graphs:
  - The server was up in 150 s, with 40.07 GiB of weights per GPU and a KV cache of 1,126,639 tokens.
  - Chat 3/3 coherent; needle-in-a-haystack 4/4 (2.4K-14.4K tokens).
  - One stream 109.8 tok/s; 32 concurrent 2,112.8 tok/s.
- **Batch of 8 vs single request:** 4/8 identical. All 8 take the same path until one near-tie word ("I should provide" vs "I should list"), which comes from batch-size-dependent bf16 rounding in the batched MoE/all-reduce. The other 4 are identical to the end.

### Inkling 2 Small on A100 (no code changes needed)

Inkling 2 Small (official NVFP4 + MXFP8 checkpoint, ~393 GB) also runs on A100 with #69165's code as is. It was served with TP8 across two 4x A100-SXM4-80GB nodes: NVLink NV4 within each node, 50 Gb/s Ethernet between nodes, no cross-node NVLink.
- Settings: `--max-model-len 16384`, with `--no-numa-bind` as a workaround for the headless-node NUMA race fixed in #69978.
- The custom all-reduce is disabled ("multi-node group does not share an NVLink fabric"), so the all-reduce uses PyNCCL.

**Unit tests (one node, 4x A100):** `pytest tests/models/inkling2 -q -rs`: `295 passed, 83 skipped, 17 warnings in 1070.58s (0:17:50)`. The 4-GPU tests run here. The remaining all-reduce/DSpark skips are missing kernels (fused all-reduce for Hopper/SM10x only, no FlashInfer fusion), not GPU count.

**End to end, TP8 across 2 nodes, CUDA graphs on.** Each run checks:
- 3 greedy chat prompts
- needle-in-a-haystack retrieval at 2,442 / 4,842 / 9,642 / 14,442 prompt tokens
- 8 concurrent requests matching the single-request outputs
- decode throughput at 32 concurrent x 128 output tokens

| configuration | chat | needle | batch-8 = bs1 | 1 stream (tok/s) | 32 concurrent (tok/s) | KV cache (tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reasoning parser + DSpark | 3/3 | 4/4 | 8/8 | 112.3 | 582.2 | 51,990 |
| reasoning parser, no DSpark | 3/3 | 4/4 | 8/8 | 77.3 | 770.1 | 69,421 |

DSpark's mean acceptance length was 3.27-3.62 (server metrics). The drafter helps a single stream (1.45x) but costs throughput at high concurrency (0.76x at 32 concurrent). Decode here is network-bound: Inkling 2 Mini at TP4 on one of these nodes reaches 1,620 tok/s at 32 concurrent.

Load: 46.28 GiB of weights per GPU, 207-248 s to load from NFS (cold page cache), CUDA-graph capture 17-33 s.

## Why this is not a duplicate

On current `main`, Inkling (v1) does not run on A100, because its attention raises `NotImplementedError` below SM90. This PR fixes that without adding an attention kernel: it routes SM8x to the Inkling 2 Triton kernel from #69165, and it is validated end to end on the released Inkling-Small-NVFP4 checkpoint.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code changes, the test runs and this description.

## Not tested

- Inkling (v1) contexts above 65,536 tokens, although the KV cache would hold about 1.1M tokens. Inkling 2 Small contexts above 16,384 tokens.
- Vision input, tool-calling quality, and lm_eval accuracy on this setup.
- 8x A100 single nodes, and InfiniBand or faster links between nodes.
