</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Kimi K3: accept strict tool schemas with a `$ref` into their own property tree
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A strict Kimi K3 tool whose parameters use a `$ref` into their own property tree (for example `#/properties/config/properties/limit`) is rejected with HTTP 400 on the Python frontend. This PR makes such schemas compile and be enforced.

One commit, `ba2e60a4ee`, on base `ab1c06419c`. No linked issue; related open PR: #62404 (different `$ref` case, see Details).

## Claims

- Strict K3 tool schemas with a JSON-pointer `$ref` into the parameters' property tree are accepted and enforced instead of failing structural-tag validation.
- `"$ref": "#"` now resolves to the parameters root. On main it is accepted but resolves to the sliced argument, so a valid call is rejected by the grammar.
- Schemas without such refs produce the same structural tag as before. `#anchor` and external refs are not rewritten.

## Validation

All runs below are CPU only, Python frontend, xgrammar 0.2.9.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  tests/tool_use/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_kimi_k3_named_tool_choice.py -q
# 382 passed (at ba2e60a4ee)

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py
# all hooks passed (ruff, typos, mypy, test tethering, docstring style)
```

The compiled extensions came from a main build at 8c17e4692a. The tool-parser sources are identical between that commit and the base.

<details>
<summary>New test fails on the base, passes with the fix</summary>

`test_kimi_k3_property_tree_ref_compiles_and_constrains` (5 cases), with `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py` taken from the base:

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -q -k property_tree_ref
E   RuntimeError: [...] json_schema_converter.cc:5088: Cannot find field 'config' in #/properties/config/properties/limit
FAILED ...[{"limit": 1, "same": 2, "tag": "x", "alias": 3}-True]
FAILED ...[{"limit": 1, "same": "2", "tag": "x", "alias": 3}-False]
FAILED ...[{"limit": 1, "same": 2, "tag": 3, "alias": 3}-False]
FAILED ...[{"root": {"config": {"limit": 1}}}-True]
FAILED ...[{"root": {"config": {"limit": "1"}}}-False]
5 failed, 282 deselected
```

With the fix:

```text
5 passed, 282 deselected
```

On the base all five cases fail at grammar compilation because of the property-tree ref. To see the `"$ref": "#"` behaviour on its own, I ran the same schema with only the `#` ref:

| Value for `config` (`root` is `{"$ref": "#"}`) | base | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"root": {"config": {"limit": 1}}}` (valid) | rejected | accepted |
| `{"root": {"limit": 1}}` (invalid) | accepted | rejected |
| `{"root": {"config": {"limit": "1"}}}` (invalid) | rejected | rejected |
</details>

### Request-path check with the K3 tokenizer (CPU, no generation)

The Kimi Vendor Verifier (KVV) `tool_call_json_schema` requests were sent through the real chat render path with the K3 tokenizer, followed by structural-tag validation and grammar compilation. Each schema is one request, run once on each side.

| Request set | base | this PR (`ba2e60a4ee`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 213 schemas accepted | 209 | 213 |
| rejected | `TestReferences:19`, `20`, `21`, `22` | none |
| 32 validator cases (28 must accept, 4 must reject) | 26 pass / 6 fail | 26 pass / 6 fail |

The 6 failing validator cases are the same on both sides and are not addressed here (see Details).

### Live server (earlier form of the fix, not this branch)

Kimi K3 on 8x AMD MI355X, Python frontend, KVV `tool_call_json_schema` suite, 490 items (each case streaming and non-streaming), n = 1 run per server.

| Server | Passed | Failed | `TestReferences:19-22` (8 items) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stock | 466 | 24 | 8 fail |
| stock + `--tool-strict-level parameter` | 468 | 22 | 8 fail |
| fix tree | 474 | 16 | 0 fail |

Limits of these numbers:

- They were measured on a development build based on main as of 2026-11-07, not on this branch.
- The fix tree carried an earlier two-pass form of the same rebase, plus unrelated K3 frontend fixes. The code in this PR is a simplified single-pass version.
- The 8 `TestReferences` items are the only ones that move for a deterministic reason.

### Not run

- No GPU or server run of this exact branch. This branch on current main was validated on CPU only.
- No test through `RemoteOpenAIServer`: the rejection happens at request validation in the engine, which needs a served K3 checkpoint, and that is too large for CI. The new test goes through `get_model_structural_tag` and `Grammar.from_structural_tag`, the same level as the existing K3 tests in that file. `tests/tool_parsers` is already selected by the Buildkite tool-parser step.
- The Rust frontend was not checked for the same problem. It builds K3 argument grammars with separate code.

## Details

**Root cause.** The K3 structural-tag builder embeds each argument's schema on its own and re-attaches only the root `$defs` / `definitions` tables. A ref such as `#/properties/config/properties/limit` then points at a path that no longer exists in the embedded schema, and xgrammar rejects the request.

**Fix.** When the parameters contain a JSON-pointer ref (`#` or `#/...`) that targets something other than the root `$defs` / `definitions`, the builder attaches the whole parameters document under `$defs/__k3_parameters` and prefixes those refs with that path. Only arguments that themselves use a JSON-pointer ref get the document. All other arguments, and all tools without such a ref, keep the existing embedding. Values under `const`, `enum`, `default` and `examples` are data and are not rewritten, and a property that is named `$ref` is treated as a property.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs on 2026-11-24 for `kimi k3 tool`, `kimi_k3`, `structural tag $ref`, `structural_tag_registry`, `K3 strict tool`, `Invalid structural tag specification`, `kimi $ref` and `property-tree ref`, plus the matching issue searches. No open PR or issue covers this case.

- #62404 (open) resolves the type of an argument that is declared only through a `$ref` into root `$defs` / `definitions`. It leaves the parameters unchanged when any ref points elsewhere, and its tests keep `#/properties/...` permissive. It changes `kimi_k3_tool_parser.py`, not the registry. Its diff applies cleanly on top of this branch, and with it applied the `$ref` tests of both PRs pass together (`-k ref` over the two K3 test files: 38 passed).
- #67021 (open, approved) and #66354 (open) change the K3 tool parser's streaming path and do not touch the registry. Both diffs apply cleanly on top of this branch.
- #67031 (open) edits the same registry file for whitespace caps. Its diff applies cleanly on top of this branch.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- Size. The parameters document is embedded once per argument that uses a JSON-pointer ref. In a CPU probe with 60 object arguments, adding one argument with a property-tree ref grew the structural tag from 71 kB to 128 kB. If every argument uses refs, the tag grows with (number of arguments) x (schema size).
- An argument with no single `type` (for example only a `$ref`, a union, or `anyOf`) still gets the permissive argument tag, as on main. That is the case #62404 works on. 43 of the 213 schemas above get this fallback on both sides.
- `#anchor` refs are only kept from being rewritten. xgrammar 0.2.9 warns on them and leaves the value unconstrained, on main and here.
- A dangling ref (`#/properties/missing`) is still rejected with 400.
- No docs change: no new flag, field, or default.

<details>
<summary>Edge cases probed (CPU, 13 schemas)</summary>

| Schema | base | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#/properties/...` ref inside a typed argument | 400 | accepted |
| same, together with root `definitions` refs | 400 | accepted |
| ref to a sibling string argument (`items: {"$ref": "#/properties/s"}`) | 400 | accepted |
| JSON-pointer-escaped key (`a~1b`) | 400 | accepted |
| `"$ref": "#"` | accepted, resolves to the sliced argument | accepted, resolves to the parameters root |
| `$anchor` + `"$ref": "#name"` | accepted | accepted |
| root `$defs` refs only, external ref, property named `$ref`, `$ref` inside `const` data, argument-local `$defs` with no property-tree ref | accepted | accepted |
| dangling `#/properties/missing` | 400 | 400 |
| argument-local `$defs` referenced as `#/$defs/L`, plus a property-tree ref elsewhere | 400 | 400 |

Both columns were run on the 13-schema set: `ba2e60a4ee` accepts 11 and rejects 2; the same tree with the registry file taken from the base accepts 7 and rejects 6.

The last row is not valid JSON Schema: `#/$defs/L` names the root table, which does not exist.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Remaining failures in the suites above (not addressed here)</summary>

- `bound_minimum_conflict`, `bound_min_items_conflict`: xgrammar rejects `minimum > maximum` and `minItems > maxItems`; the reference validator accepts them.
- Four `recursion_*_reject` cases: the reference validator rejects non-terminating recursive schemas; vLLM accepts them with a permissive argument.
- The other live-suite failures were not re-analysed for this PR.
</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Hy4-flash Engram: hash padded-vocab ids as pad, reject microbatching
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #69403. Two fixes for the Hy4-flash Engram n-gram hash.

Why it matters:

- vLLM accepts prompt token ids up to `vocab_size - 1` and samples over all 120832 rows, so the padded ids 120818..120831 can reach the model. For each one, and for the two tokens after it, vLLM used different Engram embedding rows than the reference model, so the model got a different Engram input than in transformers, with no error. With this PR these positions hash exactly like the reference.
- `--ubatch-size` / `--enable-dbo` were accepted for Hy4-flash Engram and then failed at start-up with a DeepGEMM assertion that does not point at the cause. Even past that crash, later microbatches would hash the wrong previous tokens. Users now get the same clear config error as DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram.

## Claims

- Ids past the checkpoint's frozen token map (vocabulary padding 120818..120831) now hash as `lookup_table[engram_pad_id]`, as in the reference, instead of through an identity map whose values also exceed the int64 bound of the hash multipliers.
- `--enable-dbo` / `--ubatch-size > 1` are rejected for Hy4-flash Engram at config time, like DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram. Before, the config was accepted and the engine failed at start-up in the DeepGEMM indexer; the microbatch path also passes the full-batch `lookback_token_ids` to every microbatch.

## Validation

On main f2f1fb71d, H200, precompiled wheel.

Unit tests, fix tests on the base commit (test hunks only) and with the fix:

```
pytest -v tests/models/hy_v4/test_flash_engram_lookup.py tests/test_config.py -k "engram_rejects_microbatching or ids_past_lookup"
base: 9 failed, 4 passed   (pad-id test; 8 HYV4Flash/VL cases: DID NOT RAISE)
fix:  13 passed
```

GPU, real `lookup_table` of tencent/Hy4-flash-FP8 and the real Triton hash kernel, one request containing every padded id, compared row by row with the reference hash:

```
base: rows differing from the reference: 42 of 104 (all 42 inside a padded id's n-gram window)
fix:  rows differing from the reference: 0 of 104
```

Config check, `EngineArgs(model=<Hy4-flash-FP8>, tensor_parallel_size=4, ubatch_size=2).create_engine_config()`:

```
base: accepted; at start-up every TP worker fails in microbatch 0:
      Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:278): _schedule_meta_size == num_sms / num_kv_multicast + 1
fix:  ValueError: ... Engram does not support DBO or microbatching. Disable --enable-dbo and set --ubatch-size to 0.
```

Hy4-flash is not in CI (checkpoint size), so the GPU checks above were run by hand.

## Details

Root causes: `FlashEngramLayout.load_lookup` extended the map with `range(len(map), vocab_size)`; the reference reads ids `>= lookup_table.shape[0]` as the pad id. `slice_model_inputs` does not slice `lookback_token_ids`, and the Flash hash reads lookback rows by microbatch-local request index. Rejecting microbatching matches the existing DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram check; slicing the lookback per microbatch can come later if microbatching becomes supported for Flash.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][KV Connector][Mooncake] Support HiSparse host-pool imports
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Support Mooncake KV imports from an ordinary sparse-MLA prefiller into a HiSparse decoder. The prefiller may store source KV and indexer KV in one cache group, while the decoder stores source KV in host memory and indexer KV on the GPU. Mooncake previously rejected these different group layouts.

The change reuses Mooncake's existing region planner, matching regions by layer and pairing pages using each endpoint's own group IDs. Each decoder group imports its uncached suffix. For a shared host pool, only decoder TP rank 0 registers and requests host writes; every rank retains its GPU-indexer transfer and completion obligation.

Different P/D TP sizes use the existing replicated-MLA sender selection and completion counting. Enabling this only removes the equal-TP restriction from the new import path. No transfer metadata fields, kernels, or completion-aggregator changes are added.

## Supported scope

Sparse MLA, PP=1, matching token block sizes, and unsplit physical pages. Asymmetric TP follows Mooncake's existing divisible-size requirement, for example TP2 → TP4 or TP4 → TP2.

Page pairing requires each decoder group's missing pages to be a contiguous logical suffix: P supplies its last N blocks for D's N requested blocks. Groups may have different prefix-hit lengths. Interior holes and window-clipped page sets are outside this path's contract; supporting them would require logical page positions rather than pairing by count.

## Validation

- **GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8 → TP8 (`c097fa5740`), 16 H200:** cold imports at 129/513/1025 tokens and matched-history prefix growth (129 → 513 → 1025 → repeat) exactly matched P replay token IDs and returned logprobs (delta 0). The 5074-token lookup returned the expected `50`. Transfer metrics recorded 924,936,192 bytes and 22,296 descriptors, with zero connector failures.
- **GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8 → TP16 (`81cae623df`), 24 H200:** real imports and prefix growth completed, with 12,235,788,288 transferred bytes, 53,328 descriptors and zero connector failures. 
- **Current-revision HiSparse unit cases: 126 passed, 22 deselected**, with teardown warnings. Coverage includes producer TP1/2/4 and decoder TP1/2/4/8, packed/separate storage, shared/private host pools, and non-selected producer ranks emitting no writes. Cases check copied bytes and unchanged padding.
- Ruff lint/format, Python syntax, documentation JSON, and `git diff --check` passed.

Both real-weight runs used PP1, eager execution, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, prefix caching, and a 32-GiB HiSparse host-cache budget with device buffer 2048. 

## Related work

This addresses the HiSparse host-pool import portion of #60523. The earlier duplicate-work check found no open PR providing these imports; #64871 concerns shared descriptor planning and #62504 concerns layer/chunkwise transfer.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, documentation, and this description. The author reviewed and validated the change.

commits.pr_title: [Model][Qwen4Exp] Apply an online quantization target to the lm_head
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`Qwen4ExpForCausalLM` builds its lm_head without the quant config. So a `quantization_config.targets` entry that names the lm_head (the documented way to quantize a head online, see "Quantizing the lm_head" in `docs/features/quantization/online.md`) is silently dropped on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: no error, no log line, and the head stays BF16. Part of the verify-side discussion in #68711.

## Claims

- `--quantization-config '{"targets":{"re:.*lm_head$":{"weight":"fp8_per_channel_static"}}}'` now quantizes the Qwen4Exp lm_head. It saves 0.59 GiB on nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4.
- Without a target that names the head, nothing changes. The head keeps `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` and the low-latency GEMM swap.

## Validation

Unit tests on 5aea30579a (the `nightly-5aea3057` image, with this change mounted), RTX 5090 (SM120):

```
pytest -v tests/models/test_qwen4_exp_online_lm_head.py
4 passed in 7.53s
```

Stock `nightly-5aea3057` fails at collection (the helper does not exist).

End to end on 1x DGX Spark (GB10), nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 at fc694b54, MTP k=3, nightly f2f9edca with this change:

- Model load, same server flags: BF16 72.82 GiB. With the FP8 target and without this change it is also 72.82 GiB, so the head stays BF16. With this change it is 72.23 GiB.
- Head quality: I saved the BF16 lm_head inputs from one server (9 languages of teacher-forced text, plus 2,700 Global-MMLU questions) and applied the BF16 and FP8 heads to the same inputs. The BF16 head reproduces the server's logprobs exactly over 370,665 positions. FP8 gives a mean KL of 0.0015 to 0.0049 vs BF16 per language, top-1 agreement of 0.967 to 0.984, and Global-MMLU within 1.6 points of BF16 in every language.
- Speed, sampled (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, a fixed seed per request), 12 interleaved launches, the same weights + KV budget per arm, medians of 3: output tok/s goes from 31.2 to 35.1 at c=1 (+12.5%), from 64.6 to 70.9 at c=4 (+9.8%), and +11.5 to +12.6% at c=8 to 32. The MTP drafter shares the head, so it reads the FP8 head too.

## Details

Qwen3.5 passes `quant_config=self.quant_config` to its head directly. Here that changes the unquantized case: ModelOpt resolves the excluded head to `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, and `enable_qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm` swaps only a head whose method is `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. So `_online_lm_head_quant_config` passes the config only when `online_quantization_config.resolve_quant_method_cls` selects the head. Otherwise the head is built as before. It sets `packed_modules_mapping` on the online config first, the same as `resolve_quant_method` in `base_config.py`.

Not a duplicate: the open lm_head PRs (#69574, #67236, #69177, #69434, #67897) handle the drafter's copy, defaults or kernels, and none of them changes how Qwen4Exp builds its head. An NVFP4 head also needs #70215.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, run the tests and cells, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Support grouped 4D KV cache blocks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix MoRI-IO registration for 4D attention caches split into smaller kernel blocks. With Qwen3-32B and AITER FA, a 64-token scheduler block contains two 32-token kernel blocks, but MoRI-IO rejects the cache with `Unsupported MoRIIO K/V cache shape`.

Also handle AITER's shuffled K/V planes, whose V offsets depend on each server's cache pool size.

## Claims

- Reuse `group_kernel_blocks()` to calculate the block count, stride and transfer size for a complete scheduler block.
- Keep head-count and content-size validation, and reject incomplete groups, overlapping pages and transfers outside the allocation.
- Register and transfer shuffled K/V planes using each peer's pool size, without treating the two planes as two attention heads.
- Cover both `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=0` and `=1` with byte-copy unit tests and Qwen READ/WRITE serving regressions.

## Validation

Latest validation used **AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950)** with Qwen/Qwen3-32B, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, AITER enabled and AITER linear enabled. MORI/UMBP: `1.2.3.post1` (the upstream pin); AITER: `0.1.30+rocm10.0.0.torch2.13.31f72a4.d20261120`.

**1,307 unit tests, three Qwen server regressions per shuffle setting, and pre-commit passed.** Shuffle `0` used block size 64 with grouped 32-token kernel blocks; shuffle `1` used block size 16 with unsplit K/V planes. Both READ and WRITE were tested.

**Latest accuracy run:** full Qwen3-32B weights, TP1 per prefill/decode server, MoRI-IO READ/xGMI, block size 16 and `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`. Each UMBP mode ran the same 32 NIAH questions twice at **32,768 input tokens**, using temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95 and a 2,048-token output budget. Default thinking behavior was preserved. The lm_eval chat adapter used serial requests with its default concurrency.

1. Start with a fresh UMBP store and capture both servers' metrics.
2. Run `lm_eval` once, then capture metrics again.
3. Reset both GPU prefix caches with `reset_external=false`, keeping UMBP data, and capture metrics after reset.
4. Repeat the same questions and cache salts, then capture final metrics and compare individual answers.

| UMBP mode + MoRI-IO PD | Pass 1 accuracy | Pass 2 accuracy | GPU hit rate, pass 1 / 2 | UMBP hit rate, pass 1 / 2 | Pass 2 completed UMBP loads |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Embedded | 32/32 | 32/32 | 0% / 0% | 0% / 99.95% | 65,504 |
| Standalone | 32/32 | 32/32 | 0% / 0% | 0% / 99.95% | 65,504 |

All 32 returned answers matched between passes in each mode. Both GPU resets succeeded; pass 2 recorded **zero GPU hits and zero UMBP load failures**. UMBP restored 1,048,064 of 1,048,576 prompt tokens, transferring 255.875 GiB per mode. Metrics came from vLLM's `/metrics`, including UMBP load counters; this MORI version has no standalone metrics endpoint.

Hit rates use per-pass `/metrics` counter deltas: `100 × hits / queries`. These table columns are from **prefill**; decode's external-hit counters measure MoRI-IO transfer, not UMBP reuse.

The earlier TP2 dummy-model sweep started and transferred successfully in both modes, but failed its numerical comparison: repeated GPU-cached controls also varied. This PR does not claim to fix that instability or establish TP2 accuracy.

<details>
<summary>Unit and server regression checks</summary>

The initial regression cases failed before the fix and passed afterward:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_kv_layout.py -k packed_kernel_blocks -q
```

```text
Before: ValueError: Unsupported MoRIIO K/V cache shape for layer layer: (12, 2, 16, 8)
8 failed, 6 passed, 50 deselected, 14 warnings in 4.05s
After:
14 passed, 50 deselected, 14 warnings in 3.74s
```

The expanded layout tests exercise actual allocator views and copy complete blocks between buffers, checking neighboring blocks and allocation boundaries. Compact-layout tests cover 16/32-token kernel blocks, unsplit 64-token blocks, both shuffle settings, padding and offsets. The new shuffled-plane test uses actual `LHBNC` views and different source/destination pool sizes, including one-block pools. It checks registration size and copies the last K/V block without touching neighboring blocks.

Before the shuffled-plane fix, the new unit reproducer requested 786,432 registration bytes from a 393,216-byte allocation. The shuffled Qwen serving reproducer failed engine startup with `shared KV backing too small for MR`. Both pass after the fix. WRITE also required correcting the packed-plane head metadata, which previously described the two K/V slots as two heads.

The latest runtime and test code is committed as `4657bb06bbf13acf8a4d5a3ef204fffe09558ab5`, based on upstream `c2cc003c5b644095cabcd5212d2967546ce344f8`. The initial grouped-block before/after reproducer above used base `8399da37800dfa13d19e116cb2c838aa33538320` plus the fix where applicable.

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES= ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio -q
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/moriio_integration/test_write_dummy_e2e_rocm.py -k 'qwen3_dense_aiter and not shuffled' -v -s
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/moriio_integration/test_write_dummy_e2e_rocm.py -k qwen3_dense_aiter_shuffled -v -s
```

```text
Full MoRI-IO unit suite, including the final layout cases:
1307 passed, 21 warnings in 395.34s (0:06:35)
Shuffle=0 server regressions:
3 passed, 39 deselected, 14 warnings in 240.01s (0:04:00)
Shuffle=1 server regressions:
3 passed, 39 deselected, 14 warnings in 235.04s (0:03:55)
```

The server regressions cover READ, WRITE and deliberately corrupted prefill KV for both shuffle settings. READ and WRITE matched the direct server's first-token scores exactly; the corruption control was detected. Existing MoRI-IO CI jobs select these test files. Pre-commit checks passed during the commit.

Each completed real-weight `lm_eval` pass reported:

```text
|  Tasks  |Version|Filter|n-shot|    Metric     |   |Value|   |Stderr|
|---------|------:|------|-----:|---------------|---|----:|---|-----:|
|niah_umbp|      1|none  |     0|needle_accuracy|↑  |    1|±  |     0|
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Complete serve and accuracy commands</summary>

Run from the vLLM checkout in an environment with vLLM, AITER and MORI/UMBP installed. The commands use example GPUs 0/1, loopback ports and temporary sockets; run one UMBP mode at a time. Each server runs in a separate terminal. For standalone mode, make MORI's `umbp_standalone_server` executable available on `PATH`. The UMBP pool is 384 GiB of host DRAM.

Common environment in each server terminal:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1 VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_HOST_IP=127.0.0.1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export UMBP_DRAM_PREFAULT=0
mkdir -p /tmp/moriio-layout-test
```

Start the PD proxy in another terminal:

```bash
.venv/bin/python examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 36367
```

**Embedded UMBP — prefill:**

```bash
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_PORT=15300 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B --revision 9216db5781bf21249d130ec9da846c4624c16137 --tokenizer-revision 9216db5781bf21249d130ec9da846c4624c16137 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --block-size 16 --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 34816 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --language-model-only --enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details --reasoning-parser qwen3 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --seed 0 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"UMBPStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mode":"embedded","total_capacity_bytes":412316860416,"dram_prefault":false,"load_async":true,"lookup_async":false,"lookup_dir":"/tmp/moriio-layout-test","lookup_instance":"prefill"}},{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"xgmi","read_mode":true,"host_ip":"127.0.0.1","proxy_ip":"127.0.0.1","proxy_ping_port":"36367","http_port":"8001","handshake_port":"15700","notify_port":"15900"}}]}}'
```

**Decode — same command for either mode:**


From the [compatibility harness](https://github.com/EmbeddedLLM/amd-vllm-compatibility) checkout, with its lm_eval environment active, run the command for the selected mode. Each invocation runs both passes and resets the two GPU prefix caches between them:

```bash

export NIAH_TOKENIZER_REVISION=9216db5781bf21249d130ec9da846c4624c16137

unset UMBP_METRICS_URLS
```

```bash

```


</details>

## Details

The cache tensor counts kernel blocks, while scheduler block IDs count larger blocks. Grouping the tensor first makes registration and transfer offsets refer to the same unit. A request can then restore its prefix from UMBP on prefill and forward the complete KV blocks to decode through MoRI-IO.

For shuffled storage, all K blocks precede all V blocks. MoRI-IO registers the allocation once and transfers K and V separately using each peer's own plane offset. The two physical K/V slots are not exposed as logical attention heads.

Prefill and decode must use matching layouts and equal TP for these paths. Shuffled planes require unsplit blocks; the tested Qwen3 BF16 configuration uses block size 16. This change does not add conversion between layouts or head slicing for heterogeneous-TP transfers.

Related [PR #60783](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60783) addresses single-head MLA/indexer splits and explicitly rejects multi-head splits. This change addresses multi-head AITER FA caches with matching peer layouts. The implementations overlap in the grouping helper and need coordination before merging.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Inkling2] Read the conv cache in short_conv prefill tiles that end in padding
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Inkling 2's Triton `short_conv` skips loading the conv cache for prefill tiles (steps over 256 tokens) where no token is among the first `W - 1` of its request. It decided this from the request start of the tile's last row. Padding rows have request start 0, so in a tile that ends in padding, the check failed even when a real row in the same tile continues earlier context. That row then convolved zeros instead of its cached inputs.

This PR takes the largest request start in the tile instead. Real rows have non-decreasing starts, so the maximum is the last real row's start, and padding no longer hides it.

This kernel runs in the standard executor's unfused hidden-stream convolution, which includes TP=1 on any GPU, and in the SM12x `conv_mix` fallback. The loop executor (Inkling 2 Mini) takes `conv_mix` even at TP=1, so outside SM12x it uses the native fused kernel instead. Split out of #69165 (fix by @Ar4ikov), so it can land on its own.

## Claims

- **Padded prefill steps now match the full-sequence reference** (within the test's existing tolerance). The new padded schedule fails on `main` (max abs diff 2.5-3.6) and passes with this change.
- **Nothing changes for tiles without padding.** Over real rows, the largest start is the last row's start, so the decision is the same as before.

## Validation

1x B300, at `main` `671026462`.

```bash
pytest tests/models/inkling2/test_core_ops.py -q
# 67 passed, 4 skipped
```

Without the `sconv.py` change, the new cases fail:

```
FAILED tests/models/inkling2/test_core_ops.py::test_short_conv_chunked_matches_full_sequence[steps2-False]
FAILED tests/models/inkling2/test_core_ops.py::test_short_conv_chunked_matches_full_sequence[steps2-True]
Greatest absolute difference: 2.46875 at index (2, 47) (up to 0 allowed)
```

`test_short_conv_chunked_matches_full_sequence` now appends 3 padding rows to every step and gains a `PADDED_STEPS` schedule: a long step ending in a request that continues earlier context, so the last tile with real tokens ends in padding rows. CI runs it in the `(B200) Inkling` step.

No end-to-end run: the bug needs a specific batch layout (a continuing request in the last tile of a padded step over 256 tokens), and the kernel test reproduces exactly that.

AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) was used.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Leave the shard coverage check out of /ci retry on a new commit
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A `/ci retry` on a new commit forwards the previous build's failed step keys in `VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS`. When "Check every test ran" (`runtime-shard-coverage-check`) is one of them, ci-infra's pipeline generator fails bootstrap with `Unknown CI step key(s): runtime-shard-coverage-check`, and nothing runs. The generator adds that check itself for the sharded steps a build runs, so the bot no longer forwards it.

## Claims

- `/ci retry` on a new commit no longer forwards `runtime-shard-coverage-check`. The retry build runs the other failed steps, and ci-infra adds the coverage check back when one of them is sharded.

## Validation

Incident: Buildkite [CI #105819](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105819), a `/ci retry` on #69955. Its source build #105802 failed `examples`, `plugin-tests-2-gpus` and `runtime-shard-coverage-check`. From the bootstrap log:

```
only_step_keys: frozenset({'runtime-shard-coverage-check', 'examples', 'plugin-tests-2-gpus'})
ValueError: Unknown CI step key(s): runtime-shard-coverage-check
```

I ran the ci-infra generator (main 6798f40a) locally in a vLLM checkout at main ebe4901d02 (#105819's merge base), with `aws`, `docker` and `buildkite-agent` stubbed:

```bash
BUILDKITE_BRANCH=lucamotz:tfb-resolve-model-type BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST=false \
  VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS="$KEYS" \
  pipeline-generator --pipeline_config_path .buildkite/ci_config.yaml --output_file_path pipeline.yaml
```

- Keys main's bot sends, `["examples","plugin-tests-2-gpus","runtime-shard-coverage-check"]`: `ValueError: Unknown CI step key(s): runtime-shard-coverage-check`.
- Keys this PR sends, `["examples","plugin-tests-2-gpus"]`: exit 0. The pipeline has `image-build`, `examples` (2 shards), `plugin-tests-2-gpus` and `runtime-shard-coverage-check`, which depends on `examples`.

New unit test, Python 3.12, from the repository root:

```bash
python -m pytest .github/workflows/scripts/test_run_ci_command.py -q -k shard_coverage
```

main (ebe4901d02) with the new test:
```
E       AssertionError: Lists differ: ['examples', 'runtime-shard-coverage-check'] != ['examples']
FAILED .github/workflows/scripts/test_run_ci_command.py::RunCiCommandTest::test_ci_retry_new_head_leaves_shard_coverage_check_to_ci_infra
1 failed, 95 deselected in 0.06s
```

PR (9aa4d2394b):
```
1 passed, 95 deselected in 0.04s
```

The whole file on the PR: `96 passed, 157 subtests passed in 3.09s`. The `CI command tests` workflow runs this file. pre-commit passes.

## Details

- I fixed this in the bot because the generator already builds the coverage check from the sharded steps it selects. It also keeps its hard error for unknown keys, as vllm-project/ci-infra#520 did for the `amd-<key>` mirror keys.
- If the coverage check was the only failed step, the bot now creates no build and replies that no failed jobs need retrying. That is the reply it already gives for a source build with no failed script jobs. `/ci run` still works on the new commit.
- This does not unstick a PR that already has such a retry build on its head. `/ci retry` there reruns the failed bootstrap with the same keys. It needs a new commit or `/ci run` from someone with write access.
- Not a duplicate: #55413 (adds `bootstrap` to `SETUP_STEP_KEYS`) and #62548 (skips soft-failed jobs) change the same function but do not handle this key. vllm-project/ci-infra#951 reworks the coverage records, not the step key or `VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS`.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][Multimodal] Load processed multimodal tensors from S3 in /inference/v1/generate
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `features.kwargs_refs` to `/inference/v1/generate`. Instead of inlining an item's processed tensors as base64 `kwargs_data`, a trusted client uploads them as one SafeTensors object to an S3-compatible store and sends a small reference. The Python frontend downloads and checks the object, rebuilds the item with the model's field config, and submits the normal engine input.

This ports a change we run in Cohere's vLLM fork (written by @dongluw, co-author here), with reads allowed to run concurrently. In an RL-rollout-style benchmark behind a 4-core `vllm-router`, it raises throughput by up to 1.36× (see the benchmark below).

## Claims

- `kwargs_refs` is opt-in and parallel to `mm_hashes`, like `kwargs_data`. Items in one request can mix references, inline data and cache lookups, but one item can't set both `kwargs_data` and `kwargs_refs`.
- `kwargs_refs` are enabled at startup with `--mm-tensor-refs-config '{"s3_allowed_uri_prefix": "s3://bucket/prefix", ...}'` (a new `MMTensorRefsConfig` frontend config). The S3 client is created then, and a server started without it rejects references with a 400. The server owns the endpoint and the credentials; a reference carries only `uri`, `format`, `nbytes` and `digest`. Each object is capped by `max_object_bytes` (1 GiB) and checked against its declared length and SHA-256 before decoding. The objects of one request are capped together by `max_request_bytes` (1 GiB), checked before anything is downloaded.
- Up to `max_concurrent_reads` (default 32) requests per API server download at once, on a dedicated thread pool. Each request also reserves twice its objects' declared size (the downloaded bytes and the decoded copy) from `max_reserved_bytes` (8 GiB per API server) and keeps it until the request finishes, including a stream that's closed or dropped before it's read, and a download still running after a disconnect. Requests wait in arrival order for room.
- A disallowed reference, an oversized request, or `mm_metadata` that changes or adds fields of a referenced item returns 400. A missing, inaccessible or mismatched object returns the same 422 without its size or store status. Tensors the model's processor can't use (unknown fields, only CPU-side metadata, wrong rank, more or fewer rows than the image grid describes, negative sizes) return 422, as for media URLs. A store error or timeout returns 503.
- Behind a router, the request body drops from 1.5–32 MiB to 2–32 KiB. In the benchmark below, throughput rises by 1.02–1.36×.

## Validation

### Benchmark: RL rollouts with different image payload

We compare two ways of sending the same processed image to `/inference/v1/generate`:
- **inline:** `features.kwargs_data`, base64 in the request body.
- **refs:** `features.kwargs_refs`, pointing at a SafeTensors object in CoreWeave AI Object Storage (S3-compatible).

Both modes send the same expanded token IDs and the same tensor bytes, so the engine does the same work.

**Setup**

| | |
|---|---|
| Hardware | One node with 4× NVIDIA GB200 (186 GB each) and 144 Grace CPU cores |
| vLLM | This PR at a1a0d92455, before it was rebased on a newer `main`. 4 replicas of Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct (bf16, TP=1), one per GPU: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct --enable-scale-out --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 4`. 32 concurrent reads per API server (the default); everything else at defaults (`max_num_seqs` 1024, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, on-device image normalization) |
| Router | `vllm-router` 0.1.17 (`pip install vllm-router`) with `--policy round_robin --max-payload-size 1073741824 --request-timeout-secs 600`, pinned to 4 cores with `taskset -c 0-3`, like a gateway pod with a 4-CPU limit. Replicas and clients run on cores 16–143. |
| Object store | CoreWeave AI Object Storage, read through its LOTA endpoint. The objects are uploaded before each run. |
| Clients | 8 processes × 128 concurrent requests (aiohttp, closed loop), sending everything through the router |

**Requests.** Each request is a single-image chat prompt ("Describe this image."). It is rendered once by `/v1/chat/completions/render` and then sent with `max_tokens=1` and temperature 0. The tensors are uint8 `pixel_values` and `image_grid_thw` filled with deterministic random bytes, in the shapes vLLM's Qwen3-VL processor produces with on-device normalization.

| image | patches | prompt tokens | tensor bytes | inline body | refs body |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 448² | 784 | 210 | 1.1 MiB | 1.5 MiB | ~2 KiB |
| 1344² | 7056 | 1778 | 10.3 MiB | 13.8 MiB | ~14 KiB |
| 2048² | 16384 | 4110 | 24 MiB | 32 MiB | ~32 KiB |

**Simulated RL rollout conditions.**
- **Load:** 1024 requests are in flight (256 per replica), so every engine always has a queue, as when rollout workers keep the engines busy.
- **Objects:** every 8 consecutive requests from a client share one object, like the 8 rollouts of one prompt in an RL group. Each object is uploaded once and read only by its group's 8 requests, and no object is reused across groups or runs.
- **No encoder reuse:** every request carries its own `mm_hash`, so no encoder output is reused between requests in either mode.

**Measurement.**
- **Run shape:** each run sends 16 warmup requests per client, then 384 (448², 1344²) or 256 (2048²) measured requests per client. All clients start together.
- **Throughput:** we count requests completed in the steady part of the run, from 20% of the way in until the first client has sent all of its requests.
- **Reported values:** each cell is the median of 3 runs, alternating which mode goes first. No request failed.

**Results**

| image | inline req/s | refs req/s | refs / inline | p50 latency, inline / refs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 448² (1.1 MiB) | 1733 | **2357** | **1.36×** | 0.54 / 0.45 s |
| 1344² (10.3 MiB) | 220 | **241** | **1.10×** | 4.7 / 4.1 s |
| 2048² (24 MiB) | 72.8 | 74.4 | 1.02× | 13.4 / 13.3 s |

![inline vs kwargs_refs behind a 4-core vllm-router](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/zhxchen17/781f471b02e8a75a7e22d7f493abbe2e/raw/pr-68477-benchmark-v2.png)

- **Inline:** every request moves 1.5–32 MiB through the router, and the vLLM API servers must parse and base64-decode the body. At 448² and 1344², refs is 10–36% faster.
- **refs:** the router forwards a 2–32 KiB body, and the tensor bytes go straight from the object store to the API servers that need them.
- **At 2048²:** each request's engine work is large enough that the 4 router cores keep up, so the two modes are within 2%. The gap grows with the request rate one router serves: more replicas behind it, or a smaller CPU budget, raise the bytes it must forward per second for inline tensors, but not for refs.

### Tests

GPU, one GB200, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct:

```bash
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py
# 20 passed
```

- An image loaded from a local S3 stand-in generates the same greedy tokens as the same tensors sent inline. The referenced copy gets a new `mm_hash`, so the encoder runs on the downloaded tensors.
- `test_kwargs_refs_are_read_concurrently` blocks each GET until the other request's GET arrives. It passes by default and fails with `max_concurrent_reads` set to 1 (503 once the barrier times out), the one-read-at-a-time behavior.
- The bad prefix (400), oversized request (400), conflicting `mm_metadata` (400), missing object (422), undeclared field (422), 0-dim `pixel_values` (422), too few rows (422), too many rows (422), negative grid (422) and grid-only object (422) cases return the expected errors, and `/health` stays 200 after each. Without the flat-field check, too few rows, a negative grid and a grid-only object crash the EngineCore, a 0-dim `pixel_values` returns 500, and extra rows are silently dropped (200).
- `test_kwargs_refs_release_their_memory` runs the server with room for about three items and sends eight referenced requests in a row, half of them streamed. With reservations never released, it times out on the fourth. A CPU test also covers a stream that's closed before its first chunk, which the earlier async-generator wrapper leaked.
- `test_bad_reference_is_rejected_before_any_download` sends a valid and an out-of-prefix reference in one request and checks that the 400 comes before the valid object is read.

CPU:

```bash
pytest -q tests/multimodal/test_tensor_transport.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py \
  tests/test_envs.py \
  tests/entrypoints/common/test_cli_args.py \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py
# 428 passed
```

The whole `tests/entrypoints/scale_out` directory, as the Entrypoints Integration step runs it, on one GB200: 736 passed, 7 skipped, 1 xfailed (before the last validation-order fix, which added one e2e case).

`pre-commit run` passes, including mypy and the test-tethering check.

No accuracy eval was run: the change doesn't touch preprocessing or model code, and the GPU test compares outputs against the inline path.

## Details

- **Why:** in RL, the trainer already has the processed image tensors, and the trainer and the inference servers sit on different nodes behind a gateway. Sending tensors inline pushes every byte through the gateway and the HTTP body. Reprocessing raw images in vLLM could make training and inference disagree. SHM-based paths don't help across nodes.
- **Wire format:** one object holds one item: the tensors this server's processor produces for it, with their batch dimension (the same tensors `/render` returns in `kwargs_data`). For Qwen3-VL with on-device normalization, that means a uint8 `pixel_values`, not the Hugging Face processor's float32. `BaseMultiModalProcessor.build_mm_kwargs_from_processed_tensors` restores the field config from `_get_mm_fields_config` and rejects fields the model doesn't declare. Clients don't need vLLM, and `MultiModalKwargsItem` doesn't become part of the wire contract.
- `mm_hash` stays the cache key; the URI is only where to fetch the object.
- **Concurrency:** the first version in our fork held one `asyncio.Lock` per API server across download, hashing and decoding, so with large items the downloads became the bottleneck. Reads now run on a dedicated pool of `max_concurrent_reads` threads, so slow downloads can't take the event loop's default executor from other work. The default is 32: in our runs, fewer slots capped throughput once a read took 0.1–0.5 s. `run_in_read_slot` releases a slot from the executor future's done callback, not when the request coroutine exits. That's because a client disconnect cancels the request (`with_cancellation`) but can't stop the download thread. `test_cancelled_read_keeps_its_slot_until_the_read_finishes` fails with the plain `async with semaphore: await asyncio.to_thread(...)` pattern.
- **Memory:** a request keeps its decoded tensors until it finishes, because the frontend holds the engine input that long. So the reservation lasts until then. `serve_tokens` releases it when the response is built; a stream is wrapped in `ReleasingStream`, which releases when it ends, is closed, or is garbage-collected unread. The read thread holds the reservation too, so a disconnect during a download doesn't return the bytes early.
- **Read latency:** each read adds object-store latency to a request's TTFT. That latency is hidden while the engine has a queue, as in the benchmark. On a lightly loaded server, inline `kwargs_data` is faster for small items.
- **boto3:** `boto3` stays optional, imported at module level behind `PlaceholderModule` as in `vllm/transformers_utils/s3_utils.py`. Only creating the client at startup needs it; references are validated without it. The endpoint is `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` if set, otherwise the standard boto3 config, which also sets the addressing style.
- **Malformed tensors:** `build_mm_kwargs_from_processed_tensors` turns any failure into a 422. It also requires at least one field that isn't CPU-side metadata, and each flat field's slices to satisfy `0 <= start <= stop` and to end exactly at the tensor's length, because slicing would otherwise drop rows silently or count from the end. It doesn't check model-specific shapes or values: a `pixel_values` row of the wrong width, or a grid whose sizes are consistent but invalid for the model, still fails inside the EngineCore, as it does for inline `kwargs_data` today. Validating decoded features per model is out of scope for this PR; #66237 adds that validation for inline features in this endpoint.
- **Trust:** the server reads objects with its own credentials, so every caller of the endpoint can reference every readable object under the allowed prefix. The docs say so and advise one prefix per trust domain. Error responses don't reveal whether an unknown object exists or how large it is.
- **Limitations:** the Python frontend only (the Rust frontend still requires `kwargs_data` and rejects these requests). Like `kwargs_data`, it's meant for trusted clients. Frontend-to-engine IPC is unchanged. vLLM never deletes objects and doesn't cache downloads.
- **Not a duplicate:** #68071 adds local SHM file inputs to the Rust gRPC frontend (same host only), #53809 adds a server-populated Mooncake processor cache, and #64721 forwards inline features through chat. None of them loads client-uploaded tensors from object storage.
- **Size:** about 700 non-test lines (including docstrings), most of them in the new `vllm/multimodal/tensor_transport.py`, `s3_transport.py` and `vllm/config/mm_tensor_refs.py`.

AI assistance was used to port and test this change and to run the benchmark. I reviewed the diff and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #68839 (merged). Builds on #70004 (merged); against main the diff is this PR's own change only. This PR fixes a crash in HY4 VL encoder CUDA graphs when videos are disabled; the bug is in shared code and also affects NVIDIA. It also replaces the hand-built objects (`object.__new__`/`SimpleNamespace`) in the Hy4 ROCm tests with real constructors, the two test nits deferred from #68839 review.

## Claims

- With `cudagraph_mm_encoder` enabled and `limit_mm_per_prompt` video set to 0 (what the Hy4 recipes and the #68839 serve commands pass), every image batch raised `ValueError: Model returned 1 capture axis keys, expected 0`. Image batches now replay the image encoder graph. Behaviour with video enabled is unchanged on NVIDIA and ROCm.
- New regression test through `LLM.chat`: `tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py::test_hyv4_flash_vl_image_only_encoder_graphs`.
- The strict xfail for AITER's FP8 block-scale MoE ignoring `swiglu_limit` now applies only to aiter < 0.1.30 (fixed by ROCm/aiter#7019, shipped in v0.1.30), so the test passes before and after the AITER bump (#69442).
- The Hy4 ROCm tests now build `HYV4AiterMLASparseImpl`, `HYV4MLAAttention`, `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata`, `VllmConfig`/`ModelConfig`/`EngramConfig` and the Engram `HYV4FlashConfig` with their real constructors instead of `object.__new__`/`SimpleNamespace`.

## Validation

After #70004 merged, main merged in as `03cd57c3a4` (one conflict in `tests/models/hy_v4/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, resolved to this PR's `_decode_metadata(...)`), on MI350X with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`:
```
pytest tests/models/hy_v4/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py                         22 passed, 19 warnings in 30.76s
pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -k encoder_graphs                          2 passed, 20 deselected, 18 warnings in 80.06s (0:01:20)
pytest tests/models/hy_v4_flash/test_rocm_modules.py tests/models/hy_v4_flash/test_rocm_sparse_indices.py tests/kernels/test_hy_v4_flash_kernels.py
                                                                                 94 passed, 8 skipped, 3 xfailed, 19 warnings in 109.05s (0:01:49)
pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)'              3 passed, 19 deselected, 20 warnings in 162.19s (0:02:42)
```

On `0c42273f25` (stacked on #70004, before it merged), 8x MI350X (gfx950), `cd tests`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`:
```
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 pytest -v -s models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)'
3 passed, 19 deselected, 20 warnings in 161.32s (0:02:41)
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 pytest models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -m 'not distributed'
19 passed, 3 deselected, 39 warnings in 814.85s (0:13:34)
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 pytest models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -k encoder_graphs
2 passed, 20 deselected, 18 warnings in 72.75s (0:01:12)
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 pytest models/hy_v4/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py
22 passed, 19 warnings in 30.82s
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 pytest models/hy_v4_flash/test_rocm_modules.py models/hy_v4_flash/test_rocm_sparse_indices.py kernels/test_hy_v4_flash_kernels.py
94 passed, 8 skipped, 3 xfailed, 19 warnings in 102.09s (0:01:42)
```
Rebasing onto #70004 conflicted in one place: `tests/models/hy_v4/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, where #70004 added `topk_start=0` to the hand-built metadata this PR replaces with `_decode_metadata(...)`. The real `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata` defaults `topk_start` to 0, so this PR's version was kept.

Earlier, before stacking: Rebased onto main at `4f01a46268` (includes #68839 as `3a5ae75953`) as `81efaecb2a`, re-run on 2x MI350X (gfx950):
```
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py
13 passed, 1 skipped, 31 warnings in 540.58s (0:09:00)   # skip: 2-GPU test with 1 GPU visible
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -m distributed
1 passed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 37.11s
# pytest tests/models/hy_v4 tests/models/hy_v4_flash tests/kernels/test_hy_v4_flash_kernels.py
2 failed, 196 passed, 11 skipped, 3 xfailed, 19 warnings in 187.11s (0:03:07)
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -k encoder_graphs
2 passed, 12 deselected, 18 warnings in 72.80s (0:01:12)
# same, with vl_cudagraph.py from main:
ValueError: Model returned 1 capture axis keys, expected 0 (one per axis of capture_axes).
1 failed, 1 passed, 12 deselected, 18 warnings in 70.09s (0:01:10)
```
`pre-commit run` on the six changed files passes.

Earlier runs on 8x MI350X (gfx950), on top of #68839's head `879f3f0352` as `d7a95a434e`:
```
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py
13 passed, 1 skipped, 60 warnings in 234.71s (0:03:54)   # skip: 2-GPU test with 1 GPU visible
# HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -m distributed
1 passed, 13 deselected, 18 warnings in 16.98s
# pytest tests/models/hy_v4 tests/models/hy_v4_flash tests/kernels/test_hy_v4_flash_kernels.py
2 failed, 196 passed, 11 skipped, 3 xfailed, 19 warnings in 199.06s (0:03:19)
```
Development runs (on c50ff39c4c, GPUs 2 and 3):

Regression test, without the fix:
```
ValueError: Model returned 1 capture axis keys, expected 0 (one per axis of capture_axes).
1 failed, 13 deselected, 18 warnings in 17.13s
```
With the fix (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -k encoder_graphs`):
```
2 passed, 12 deselected, 21 warnings in 32.51s
```
Full suites, run twice:
```
# VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py
14 passed, 63 warnings in 261.71s (0:04:21)
14 passed, 63 warnings in 237.91s (0:03:57)
# pytest tests/models/hy_v4 tests/models/hy_v4_flash tests/kernels/test_hy_v4_flash_kernels.py
2 failed, 192 passed, 11 skipped, 3 xfailed, 24 warnings in 187.21s (0:03:07)
2 failed, 192 passed, 11 skipped, 3 xfailed, 19 warnings in 208.25s (0:03:28)
```
The 2 failures there are `tests/models/hy_v4/test_sequence_parallel.py`, which needed the CUDA-only FlashMLA backend on main; #70004 makes it run on ROCm. The 3 xfails are the known strict xfail for AITER FP8 `swiglu_limit`. `tests/models/hy_v4/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` now takes 19.95s (was 10.99s) because each test builds a real config and distributed env.

## Details

**Root cause.** `get_encoder_cudagraph_config` drops the `("image", "video")` capture axis when the video limit is 0, but `select_encoder_cudagraph_items` always returned `ENCODER_CUDAGRAPH_AXIS_KEYS_KWARG: (modality,)`. `EncoderCudaGraphManager._select_items` requires one key per capture axis. Keys are now returned only when the axis exists. With video disabled, the manager sets `max_frames_per_batch=0`, so capture already used image-shaped graphs. Other encoder-graph models (gemma4, minicpmv, deepseek_v41, kimi_k3, minimax_m3, inkling2) either always set capture axes or never return keys, so none share the bug.

**Tests.** The DFly draft impl owns no indexer (its rows are external), so with the real constructor the AITER remap is cached per metadata object. The graph-replay test therefore warms up on a fresh `dataclasses.replace(metadata)`, as the builder does each step. Without that, it fails (83.5% mismatch). Kept as stand-ins:
- The IndexPool harness config: `group_topk=6` is rejected by `HYV4FlashConfig`, which requires a 128-aligned `index_topk`.
- The `forward_mqa` layer, which only reads `_q_scale`/`_k_scale`.
- The vendor-neutral Engram `prepare_hashes` metadata.
- The DFly speculator config tests: a real `SpeculativeConfig` resolves draft and target models, which is the logic under test.

**Not changed: `hy_v4_flash/amd/swa.py` token mapping.** With `amd/engram.py` gone, the torch token-to-request/position mapping exists only in `FlashWindowIndexer.forward`. `_live_counts_kernel` and `indexpool_prepare._query_metadata` are Triton kernels with different grids and outputs, so a shared helper would remove no duplication.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list` searches for the error text and for HY4 encoder-graph/video terms only return #68839.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change. The submitter must review every changed line and re-run the tests before marking this ready.

## Overview

The renderer should receive media_io_kwargs via prompt_extras so that both the chat and completion paths can pass media_io_kwargs to the renderer.

Part of #69357

Resolve https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69357#discussion_r4691802834


## Claims

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9e8b3fb83ed4f3da1ed5376083027b14994939fc/vllm/renderers/base.py#L1398-L1401

Fix prompt_extras["media_io_kwargs"] being overwritten/lost in chat rendering on main, and unify request-level media_io_kwargs merging across chat and completion paths in BaseRenderer.

## Validation

tests/renderers/unit_tests/test_media_io_kwargs.py

## Details




**prompt_extras takes precedence over chat_params.media_io_kwargs.**
**Copy prompt_extras and prompt_dict to avoid modifying user input.**

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Run QSA prefill steps with FlashInfer on Blackwell
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On B200, QSA attention takes 26% of the GPU time of an 8K prefill step of Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). This PR runs that attention, in steps that contain a prefill, on FlashInfer's QToken-KvBlock-Sparse kernel. The kernel is already in the pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.4`, and TensorRT-LLM uses it for QSA on SM100.

The Triton kernel attends one query row at a time. The FlashInfer kernel attends 8 adjacent rows of a request over the union of their selected blocks, so the rows share each K/V load. Selections and math are unchanged, and decode-only steps keep the Triton kernel in their FULL CUDA graphs. The change is scoped to SM100/SM103 with BF16 KV and adds no option. It is ~360 lines: all model-local except a FlashInfer availability check in `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`.

**Prior work**
- **#55394 / #55430.** They tried the same idea with a custom kernel on GB10 and closed at −1.6% TTFT, since QSA was 12% of prefill there. The author left the idea open for hardware where QSA weighs more. Each request from that review is answered here:

  | Asked in #55394 | Here |
  | --- | --- |
  | Real-input microbenchmarks | Replay of indexer selections captured from a 27.9K-token prompt, 13 layers × 4 chunks |
  | Retune Triton first | The best of 48 configs is within 3% of the current one; FlashInfer is 2.4–3.7x |
  | Prefill/decode split | Only steps with a query longer than `1 + num_speculative_tokens` use FlashInfer |
  | Multi-request | Routes never cross requests; tested with a mixed step |
  | Inputs from metadata | Block IDs come from the existing selection (25 µs/layer); the indexer is unchanged |
  | Gain worth the complexity | TTFT −8% to −16%, production c32 +4.2% |

- **#56240.** A draft by the author of the QToken-KvBlock-Sparse kernel, inactive since 2026-09-14, that integrates it for prefill and decode. The main differences:

  | | #56240 | this PR |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Prefill group | 4 rows | 8 rows (1.1–1.3x faster than 4 in this PR's path, on captured selections) |
  | Plans | Cached by exact shapes and request boundaries (LRU of 4), so mixed prefill steps re-plan each layer (~0.5 ms host each) | One per (layer, row bucket), reused across steps |
  | Footprint | 1166 lines; changes indexer output and adds an env var | ~360 lines plus tests; model-local apart from an availability check |
  | Decode | Fixed MTP groups in FULL graphs: +1.4–2.2% per decode step at 64 requests (GB300) | Stays on Triton. FlashInfer is faster from 4 requests (1.1–2x per layer on B200) but slower for one (0.85x), so this PR doesn't add graph-captured plans. |

## Claims

Setup: TP1 on one B200 with production flags (NVFP4 experts, BF16 KV, MTP 3, prefix caching, chunked prefill at 8192). Load comes from `vllm bench serve`. Each arm was started twice, once per GPU with the arm order swapped, and the prefix cache was reset before each run.

| Workload | main | this PR | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Median TTFT, c1: 2K / 8K / 32K / 128K tokens (ms) | 58 / 189 / 807 / 3285 | 54 / 162 / 715 / 2945 | −8% / −15% / −11% / −10% |
| Prefill tok/s, c4: 2K / 8K / 32K | 52.2K / 49.6K / 48.3K | 58.2K / 58.7K / 56.0K | +11% / +18% / +16% |
| 8K in / 1K out, output tok/s: c4 / c16 | 782 / 1563 | 821 / 1634 | +4.9% / +4.5% |
| Production chat prompts, c32: output tok/s / p99 TTFT | 2851 / 1.75 s | 2971 / 1.50 s | **+4.2%** / −14% |

- **Kernel.** Per QSA layer on captured selections, the path is 2.0–3.4x faster, including all glue.
- **Quality.** There is no statistically clear regression (table below).
- **Costs.**
  - There is no host sync.
  - A cold FlashInfer cache pays a one-time ~80 s JIT during warmup; after that it is cached.
  - KV-cache capacity is unchanged: 2.466M vs 2.467M tokens.

## Validation

**How each number was measured**
- **Serving:** `vllm bench serve`, using the `random` dataset and, for the production rows, the `custom` dataset with a private sample of chat prompts. Commands are below.
- **Step profile:** vLLM's torch profiler (`--profiler-config`, `/start_profile`) around one 8K request.
- **Kernel:** a standalone script that replays the captured selections through both paths with random Q/K/V. It uses CUDA events and takes the median of 5 × 10 launches. The retune patches `_select_sm100_config`.
- **Quality:**
  - GSM8K and MRCR come from `tests/evals/gsm8k` and `tests/evals/mrcr`.
  - NLL comes from `prompt_logprobs` on documents built from `docs/**/*.md`: independent texts with no shared prefix.

**Tests** (B200):

```
$ pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py --durations=0
4.42s call     tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py::test_qsa_flashinfer_needs_its_jit_module[local_build]
4.25s call     tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py::test_qsa_flashinfer_needs_its_jit_module[empty]
0.75s call     tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py::test_qsa_flashinfer_matches_sparse_attention[tp1]
0.31s call     tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py::test_qsa_flashinfer_matches_sparse_attention[tp4]
113 passed, 23 warnings in 90.65s (0:01:30)
```

- `test_qsa_flashinfer_matches_sparse_attention` compares FlashInfer with the Triton kernel at TP1 and TP4.
  - It alternates a lone 32-token prompt (64-row bucket) with a mixed step: a decode with drafts, two fresh prefills and a chunked prefill. All steps share one set of buffers.
  - It runs under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`.
  - At the end it checks that dropping the buffers releases the KV cache.
- `test_qsa_flashinfer_selected_only_when_plannable` checks that FlashInfer is selected exactly for the geometries its planner accepts (5 cases).
- `test_qsa_flashinfer_needs_its_jit_module` covers `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1`, both with an empty JIT cache and with a local build of the module. In both cases FlashInfer is not selected, so the first prefill runs on Triton instead of raising `MissingJITCacheError`.
- All three run in the B200 "Qwen4 Exp Kernels" job.

**Serving on the final code.**
- Median TTFT at c1 is 53.0 ms at 2K and 162.3 ms at 8K.
- Lone prompts of 5–60 tokens and 16 concurrent short prompts run without errors.
- After the rename to FlashInfer naming in review, an in-process run with the real config and dummy weights still sends 8K prefills to FlashInfer instead of the Triton kernel (136.0 vs 155.8 ms, median of 10), with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

**Step profile** (one 8192-token request):

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU time of the step | 159.6 ms | 132.2 ms (−17%) |
| QSA attention | 41.7 ms (26%) | 10.9 ms (8%) |

The −27 ms matches the TTFT drop at 8K.

**Quality**

| Eval | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NLL, 93 docs of 3K–9K tokens | 1.22981 | −0.0004 ± 0.0005 |
| NLL, 13 docs of 30K–37K tokens | 1.19263 | +0.0001 |
| GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions | 0.914 | 0.908 (SE 0.008) |
| MRCR, 2/4/8 needles, 300 samples of 17K–34K tokens, 2 runs | 0.612 / 0.607 | 0.599 / 0.600 |

For scale, compare with kernels that compute the same thing differently. Other Triton tile configs move NLL by up to 0.0008, and MRCR by +0.002 ± 0.008. The paired MRCR difference of this PR is −0.010 ± 0.009 (1 SE).

**Host syncs.** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` reported none in serving, on either arm.

<details>
<summary>Commands and per-run numbers</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <checkpoint> --tensor-parallel-size 1 --dtype bfloat16 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":16,"video":0}' --mm-processor-kwargs '{"max_pixels":2097152}' \
  --override-generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":20,"min_p":0.0,"presence_penalty":1.5,"repetition_penalty":1.0}'

# Before each run: curl -X POST localhost:8000/reset_prefix_cache
# TTFT / prefill: L in 2048 8192 32768 131072; C=1 with 10 prompts, C=4 with 40
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len $L --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 1
# 8K in / 1K out: --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024, C=4 (24 prompts), C=16 (64 prompts)
# Production: --dataset-name custom --custom-output-len 1000 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32
# MRCR (a thin wrapper around evaluate_mrcr kept per-sample scores for the paired difference)
python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py --needles 2 4 8 --num-samples 300 --max-prompt-tokens 131072 \
  --extra-body '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false},"presence_penalty":0.0}'
# GSM8K
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0
```

Both arms use main `66e8914fc` with its precompiled wheel; the PR arm adds this commit on `PYTHONPATH`. Values are given as mean (GPU 5 run, GPU 6 run):

| Workload | main | this PR | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TTFT 2K c1 (ms) | 58.1 (59.0, 57.2) | 53.5 (53.7, 53.3) | −7.9% |
| TTFT 8K c1 | 188.9 (192.5, 185.3) | 161.5 (163.6, 159.4) | −14.5% |
| TTFT 32K c1 | 806.7 (811.1, 802.3) | 715.0 (709.1, 720.9) | −11.4% |
| TTFT 128K c1 | 3285 (3286, 3284) | 2945 (2932, 2959) | −10.3% |
| TTFT 2K / 8K / 32K c4 | 156 / 657 / 2719 | 139 / 554 / 2345 | −10.8% / −15.7% / −13.7% |
| 8K/1K c4 output tok/s | 782 (754, 811) | 821 (834, 808) | +4.9% |
| 8K/1K c16 output tok/s | 1563 (1569, 1557) | 1634 (1630, 1638) | +4.5% |
| Production c32 output tok/s | 2851 (2863, 2839) | 2971 (2978, 2965) | +4.2% |
| Production c32 p99 TTFT (ms) | 1746 (1735, 1757) | 1499 (1482, 1516) | −14.1% |
| Production c32 mean TPOT (ms) | 10.8 (10.9, 10.8) | 10.4 (10.5, 10.2) | −4.3% |
| Production, 16 output tokens, c32 output tok/s | 318 (318, 318) | 368 (369, 366) | +15.5% |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Kernel: per-layer time, Triton retune and breakdown</summary>

Mean over the 13 QSA layers of each chunk; the FlashInfer path includes route build, Q copy, block IDs and gate.

| Chunk (rows, end position) | Triton | FlashInfer, 4 rows | FlashInfer, 8 rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8000, 8000 | 3247 µs | 1201 µs (2.7x) | **945 µs (3.4x)** |
| 8000, 16000 | 3512 µs | 1655 µs (2.1x) | **1399 µs (2.5x)** |
| 8000, 24000 | 3514 µs | 1779 µs (2.0x) | **1549 µs (2.3x)** |
| 3902, 27902 | 1768 µs | 982 µs (1.8x) | **897 µs (2.0x)** |

**Triton retune.** BLOCK_N ∈ {16, 32, 64, 128} × splits ∈ {1, 2, 4} × warps ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}, first 3 layers of each chunk. The best config is (32, 2, 1) at 1.03x for the first chunk; for the other three, the current (32, 1, 1) is already the best.

**Breakdown of the FlashInfer path** (8000 rows at 8000, 825 µs):
- attention: 599 µs;
- metadata: 51 µs;
- gate: 42 µs;
- Q copy: 37 µs;
- block IDs: 25 µs;
- route build and small copies: ~70 µs. Serving builds routes once per step; this benchmark builds them per call.

</details>

## Details

- **Selection.** FlashInfer is used only when it provides the kernel and its CUDA metadata module can be loaded; otherwise the step stays on Triton. The module must ship precompiled (`flashinfer-jit-cache` does not include it), or JIT must be enabled with `nvcc` and `ninja` available. With JIT disabled, FlashInfer refuses even an up-to-date local build. The geometry must also fit:
  - a block size in {4, …, 128};
  - a head size in {64, 128, 192, 256};
  - at most 512 selected blocks per row;
  - 8 rows × query heads per KV head ≤ 128.
- **Routes.** The metadata builder builds them once per step, on the GPU, with no host sync.
  - A route is 8 adjacent rows of one request.
  - Rows are padded to a bucket (powers of two up to 1024, then multiples of 1024), so each layer reuses one plan per bucket. Preparing a plan costs ~0.5 ms of host time.
- **Plans and workspace.** Plans live in the builder's buffers, so they are released with the KV cache. All plans share one workspace, sized for the largest bucket: 21 MiB at 8192 batched tokens.
- **Per layer.**
  1. Q is copied into the bucket.
  2. Block IDs are read from the existing expanded selection.
  3. FlashInfer writes the attention.
  4. A Triton kernel applies the FP32 sigmoid gate.

---

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Cut P/D loads at the Mamba prefix-cache checkpoint
commits.pr_body: ## The Problem ## Purpose With Mamba `align` prefix caching under P/D, the decoder never holds a prefix-cacheable state for the prompt. P computes N-1 tokens and sends the running state at N-1, which is off the block grid. Retention keeps only the prompt checkpoint C (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, the default). C lives on P, so the next D-local turn of the conversation (a short follow-up, routed straight to D by conditional P/D) recomputes the whole history. #63610 measured this on Qwen3.5-9B (block 576, GSM8K multi-turn): **0 / 123,032 prompt tokens hit on D**, and 59.4% once D got the checkpoint state. This PR makes P stop its prefill **at C** and lets D recompute the tail `[C, N)` itself: - **P** (`_num_prefill_backoff_tokens`): truncates the prompt to the checkpoint a local prefill would cache. It reuses core's `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position` (exposed as `KVCacheManager.get_state_checkpoint_tokens`), so the hash lookahead and the EAGLE/MTP block drop are honoured. P's running state at C *is* the checkpoint. - **D** (`_get_remote_prefill_token_count`): mirrors P's cut. Push mode needs this, because D registers its blocks before P finishes and has no `remote_num_tokens`. In pull mode, P's `remote_num_tokens` wins on a mismatch: a heterogeneous P, or a P without this change that stops at N-1. A mismatch only costs the prefix-cache entry, never correctness. If P's recurrent state is past what D must recompute, D falls back to a local prefill. - D loads C tokens. Its own prefill of the tail then hashes C through the ordinary replay-boundary path, so the next local turn hits at C, exactly like a colocated deployment. It is always on when a Mamba group runs `align` mode with prefix caching (detected in `bind_kv_cache_manager`). Otherwise behaviour is unchanged. ### Why cut instead of shipping the checkpoint (#63610 / #66565) Both approaches leave the next turn at the same place: D hits at C and recomputes `[C, M)`. The only runtime difference is the turn that comes back from P. Here D also recomputes `N - C < block_size` tokens, once per P→D hand-off. D-local turns after that are identical. In exchange, this needs: - **no transfer-protocol change:** no extra state block, no new `kv_transfer_params`, no D-side slot that has to line up with P's; - **no retained-block lifecycle on P;** - **no requirement that P and D agree on C;** - **nothing per connector:** it works for both NIXL pull and push. ### Cost D runs the tail as a prefill chunk. That adds to TTFT and turns one step into a mixed (non-`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`) step: - **Measured step times** (Qwen3.5-122B, TP2, block size 2112): tail ≤1024 tokens takes ~24 ms, 2112 takes ~35 ms, and 4224 takes ~60 ms. - **Modelled load** (1 req/s per decoder, 70% of requests routed directly to D): ~0.7–1.0% of D's step time. The `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` step share moves from ~98.9% to ~98.5%. It mostly shows up in p99 ITL. - **Smaller blocks** (RFC #64401, 64-token blocks): the tail is at most 64 tokens and the cost is negligible. **Trade-off on P:** P now prefills up to C, so P-local reuse of the same prompt caches its state one block lower (C − block) than before. Complementary to #67053: that PR retains Mamba states crossed during decode so follow-up turns can resume past the previous output. ## Test Plan - Unit tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py`: - `test_mamba_checkpoint_cut`: P's truncation and D's load count for pull and push. Covers the cut to the checkpoint, N-1 already on the checkpoint, prompts with no checkpoint (plain N-1), and EAGLE block drop. - `test_mamba_checkpoint_cut_d_follows_prefiller`: D following P's `remote_num_tokens` when they agree, when P cuts lower, when P predates this change (N-1), and when P's state is past D's backoff. - E2E: multi-turn P/D on a hybrid Mamba model, counting D-side prefix hits on the follow-up turn. ## Test Result Unit tests added; CI pending. E2E validation to follow.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix ViT backend and custom all-reduce tests with AITER on
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_mha_attn_platform[hip]` and three tests in `test_custom_all_reduce.py` fail with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` ([#62092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62092) flips the default; seen in AMD CI build [13642](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13642)). They assumed AITER was off. This makes them pass with AITER on or off without disabling any AITER feature. Test-only.

## Claims

- `test_mha_attn_platform[hip]`: with AITER MHA on, ROCm correctly picks `ROCM_AITER_FA` for ViT attention, but the test hard-coded `FLASH_ATTN`. It now checks both outcomes.
- The eager, chunked and 1-/2-stage tests in `test_custom_all_reduce.py` are white-box tests of vLLM's `CustomAllreduce`. With AITER's all-reduce on, the TP group has none (`ca_comm` is `None`), so they crashed. They now build vLLM's `CustomAllreduce` on the same group in that case; AITER stays on. On CUDA and with AITER off they use the group's own instance, as before.
- The graph test is unchanged from `main`; with AITER on it exercises AITER's all-reduce. Its AITER-on failure in build 13642 matches [ROCm/aiter#6819](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6819), fixed in AITER v0.1.29, which `main` pins.

## Validation

MI300X, PR head, AITER 0.1.24.post1:

```bash
cd tests
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_platform distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 pytest -v kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_platform distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
```

| Test | AITER on, before | AITER on, after | AITER off, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_mha_attn_platform[hip]` | fail | pass | pass |
| `test_custom_allreduce` eager ×2, `test_custom_allreduce_chunked` ×2 | fail | pass | pass |
| `test_one_and_two_stage_allreduce_bitwise_identical` | fail ("custom all-reduce is disabled") | no longer hits the AITER failure* | * |

\* The local build predates #57042, so this test fails its bitwise check identically with AITER on and off here. Graph PP=2 with AITER on fails intermittently with AITER 0.1.24.post1 (ROCm/aiter#6819); not verified with v0.1.29.

## Details

- Not a duplicate: #62092 covers `test_fusion_pass_op_priority` and `test_auto_selection_for_kv_connector`, so they're not in this PR.
- AMD CI runs with AITER off, so it doesn't exercise these AITER-on paths; the validation above is local.
- AI assistance (Cursor agent) was used to investigate the failures and write the change.
